verdict: This bucket is two unrelated families that happened to fall in the same glob gap. Family A (27 files) is the literature anchor layer — one CSV per paper (Bazzoun x2, Bielefeld x2, Bucci x2, Chen, Cho, Cronau, Deysher, DMT, Doux, Duquesnoy, Frankenberg, Han, Hong, Huang, Jackson-Green, Jung, Kang x2, plus the interfacial-impedance, intergranular-cracking, electromechanical-contact, cycling-stress and densification records). These are immutable transcription records, nearly all committed in the 2026-06-25..07-10 litdb digest campaign, nearly all with a companion digest, and several carrying genuinely careful provenance columns (stated vs digitized, original_source_ref, explicit non-transferability warnings). They are canonical and should be kept as-is; the only defect is findability — the docs that consume their values cite PDFs and paper names, never the CSV paths, so the structured records are effectively write-only. Family B (13 files) is our own measurement output, and it splits three ways. Still canonical: esse_calibration_2mAh_real_9 (every number in the CLAUDE.md E_SE section reproduces from it), heckel_pure_se_dem, additive_test_campaign_6mAh_real_4 (quoted by live ledger CL-73), dem_input_values_20260818, densification_porosity_db. Archivable one-off studies: the six jam_* files (a June-2026 resolution-invariance sweep, complete, two of which carry a mislabelled duplicate row) and input_2mAh_a7_50_ps_sweep (complete, zero readers). And a platen-era block that needs a banner before anything is reorganized around it: a3_binder_sweep_2pressure, the mpm_porosity_pct column of case_3d_collection, and to a lesser degree dem3d_dip_sweep. That last block is where the real damage is: case_3d_collection.csv mixes eps_sphere and MPM-union porosity in adjacent columns and a live regression differences them as "plastic densification", when CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-12 correction shows the pure convention offset (-1.251 %p) exceeds the observed median difference (-0.750 %p) — the fitted signal is bookkeeping. On the ban registry: zero of the 22 quotation_ban patterns appear literally in any of the 40 files, verified by direct scan. I confirmed CSV is genuinely outside BAN_SCAN_GLOBS in scripts/check_review_findings.py (which covers md/html/js/json/pptx/docx but not csv), so this is a real gap rather than a passed check — it just happens to be clean here. One thing to record before anyone widens that sweep to CSV: docs/data/dem3d_dip_sweep.csv contains the literal token 35.79 as a porosity percent while the registry pattern is "×35.79" (a retracted sigma ratio), so a naive numeric widening would fire a false positive there. For v3: keep Family A intact and cross-link it from the consuming docs; archive the jam sweep and the a7_50 sweep; and do not carry mpm_porosity_pct or the a3 porosities forward into any new hub page without the platen banner attached to the number itself.

findings.claim: The file puts dem_porosity_pct (eps_sphere convention) and mpm_porosity_pct (MPM union convention) in adjacent columns with no note, and a live script differences them as physics. scripts/porosity_plastic_vs_rigid.py docstring: "(D) densification = dem - mpm (how much extra the plastic flow densifies)". At the median that quantity is pure bookkeeping, not plastic flow.
findings.evidence: Data file, all 155 paired rows recomputed: dem-mpm mean = -0.688 %p, median = -0.750 %p, 105/155 negative (rows: input_8mAh_real_5 16.29 vs 16.84; input_2mAh_real_5 10.23 vs 11.56; input_2mAh_real_2 11.21 vs 14.35). CONTRADICTING SOURCE — CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12 correction, echoing docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md rev6 §31: "MPM관례(16.877) − eps_sphere(15.626) = 1.251 %p" arises from lens-overlap bookkeeping alone, i.e. dem-mpm = -1.251 %p before any physics, and "모든 porosity 는 eps_sphere 로 통일해 보고할 것". Same source: in scaffold runs solid_vol is frozen at seeding from the DEM dump so "porosity 는 독립 정보를 담지 않는다" and "일치를 증명서로 쓰면 순환이다".
findings.proposed_action: Add a header note to the CSV naming the convention of each porosity column, and either convert mpm_porosity_pct to eps_sphere or subtract the per-bed lens-overlap offset before differencing. Until then, mark the (D) target in scripts/porosity_plastic_vs_rigid.py as convention-contaminated and do not report its coefficient as plastic densification.

findings.claim: Every porosity number in this file comes from the exact run class that docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md grades D (kinematic-stop defect confirmed), and the file's stated low-pressure headline finding is smaller than the documented numerical drift of the same readout. Neither the CSV nor its live doc carries a banner.
findings.evidence: Data file header: "5 MPa (<sigma_y 50): binder props -> non-monotone porosity (+0.7%p bump @0.5wt%)"; its rows give 0 wt% 16.67 -> 0.5 wt% 17.40 = +0.73 %p. Producer scripts/a3_binder_sweep.py:33-35 passes --am-scaffold ... --se-dump ... --protocol hold and reads porosity_at_target_pct (line 52). CONTRADICTING SOURCE — docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md:311 lists "real_14 se-dump hold 15.93 % · 29.95 µm | D | 결함 발동 확인(1.2프레임 물림)" — this file's 0 wt% row is 15.91 / 29.95; and §490 measures the same bed drifting 14.38 -> 12.76 -> 11.08 % on the sub-ladder alone without converging, i.e. 1.6-3.3 %p of numerical drift against the 0.73 %p claimed effect. CLAUDE.md living-track #2 lists the defect as still open (rev6, R1 result unincorporated).
findings.proposed_action: Add a banner line to the CSV and to docs/a3_binder_sweep_result.md pointing at docs/mpm_platen_kinematic_stop_defect.md, stating that the absolute porosities are stop-frame dependent and that the +0.73 %p low-P propping bump is below the documented drift of this readout. Re-run the 5 MPa arm under the corrected platen, recording each arm's stop frame, before the propping claim is used anywhere.

findings.claim: Two of the seven plastic points are marked not-equilibrated(framecap) in the data file, but the only script that reads it declares the whole sweep equilibrated, plots those points unflagged, and draws the no-Furnas-dip verdict from the resulting curve.
findings.evidence: Data file rows: "65,plastic,37.11,0.292,not-equilibrated(framecap)" and "85,plastic,35.79,0.293,not-equilibrated(framecap)". CONTRADICTING SOURCE — scripts/plot_dem3d_dip.py docstring lines 1-3: "cap ON (plastic) vs cap OFF (rigid), at EQUILIBRATED 300 MPa (fine bidirectional virial servo)"; its loader reads only mode and por_sphere and never touches the note column, and its print line asserts "plastic monotonic 39.0->34.1% (no local min)". The two flagged points sit inside the dip window the figure denies (CLAUDE.md: DEM dips at AM 70-75; de Larrard geometric dip AM 85-90).
findings.proposed_action: Make plot_dem3d_dip.py read the note column and render framecap points with an open marker plus a caption line, or re-run am=65 and am=85 plastic to equilibration. Soften the docstring from "at EQUILIBRATED 300 MPa" to "5/7 plastic points equilibrated; am 65 and 85 framecapped".

findings.claim: The AM_wt%=10 row is a bit-identical copy of the AM_wt%=20 row of the P:S 7:3 file at the same resolution — a different composition cannot produce the same material-point count and the same five porosity readouts.
findings.evidence: docs/data/jam_320_ps55.csv row 2: "10,52.0,46.44,43.3,16.0,0.2,66557". CONTRADICTING SOURCE — docs/data/jam_320.csv (P:S 7:3, the script default per scripts/mpm2d_jamming.py argparse --ps default '7:3') row 3: "20,52.0,46.44,43.3,16.0,0.2,66557" — identical in all 6 columns including n_pts. The same off-by-one duplication recurs at 512 (jam_512_ps55.csv AM=10 == jam_512.csv AM=20, both "47.4,39.99,36.6,14.5,0.1,177741"), so it is systematic, not chance; jam_320_ps37.csv AM=10 is a genuinely different row ("51.6,46.23,43.0,17.7,0.1,66901"), confirming the ps55 row is the anomaly. docs/mpm_dip_resolution_invariance.md line 88 reports the 5:5 statistics (Pearson 0.9976, shape-RMSE 1.06 %p) computed over the contaminated row.
findings.proposed_action: Re-run scripts/mpm2d_jamming.py --n-grid 320 --ps 5:5 --seeds 3 for the AM=10 point and replace the row, then recompute the 5:5 line of the composition table in docs/mpm_dip_resolution_invariance.md. If the run cannot be reproduced, blank the row and mark it missing rather than leaving a mislabelled 7:3 point inside the 5:5 file.

findings.claim: Same defect at the fine grid: the AM_wt%=10 row is a bit-identical copy of the AM_wt%=20 row of the P:S 7:3 file at n_grid 512.
findings.evidence: docs/data/jam_512_ps55.csv row 2: "10,47.4,39.99,36.6,14.5,0.1,177741". CONTRADICTING SOURCE — docs/data/jam_512.csv (P:S 7:3) row 3: "20,47.4,39.99,36.6,14.5,0.1,177741" — identical in all 6 columns including n_pts=177741; jam_512_ps37.csv AM=10 differs ("47.1,39.8,36.5,8.5,0.1,178545"). findings.claim: 155 rows of paired DEM/MPM measurements whose sole provenance is a human copy-paste of a dashboard text blob: no input_digest, no argv, no run id, no timestamp, no manifest column. Four scripts, including a production regression, read it as measurement.
findings.evidence: Data file header row is "case,mAh,ps_label,p_frac,am_wt,dem_porosity_pct,mpm_porosity_pct,..." with no provenance column. Its writer scripts/parse_case_paste.py:2-7 states: "Parse a webapp '전체 복사 (AI용)' button paste -> append/update a row in the 3D collection CSV. The paste = the full text the dashboard copy button produces", and parses by regex against UI labels. That framing appears in no prose.

surface_worthy.why: A controlled P:S sweep at fixed AM:SE with paired DEM and MPM columns is exactly the like-for-like contrast the repo keeps asking for, and this one is complete and unused — no doc, no script, absent from both canonical case tables.
surface_worthy.one_line: Orphaned complete P:S sweep (0:10 -> 10:0) at fixed AM:SE 70:30 with 41 paired DEM+MPM metrics per case.

surface_worthy.why: It is the only place that puts our porosity anchors side by side with halide, glass and LIB-wet references at matched pressures, each row carrying an explicit transferability note. A v3 reader asking "is 15.6 % reasonable" has nowhere else to look.

verdict: This bucket is not one family but three, and they are in very different health. (A) Twenty literature-anchor tables (kim/klar/kogut/lee/liu/luding/lyu/mesarovic/minnmann/mun/nam/ncm/ngandjong/nisar/oh/park/pasha) are the strongest data here: each carries a DOI header, a stated-vs-digitized precision column, and an explicit do-not-transfer caveat where the material or topology differs from ours. They are canonical and should be kept verbatim; the only problem is reachability - five (nam2026, nisar2024, minnmann2024, mun2025, liu2025) have no reader anywhere but the auto-generated inventory, and their own litdb cards never name them. (B) Six design/seal artefacts (lhs_design_20260818, lhs_ext_design v1/v2, lhs_ext_box_v2) are live and the best-governed files in the repo - v2 is sha256-verified in CI and v1 carries a self-written SUPERSEDED banner naming its replacement and reason; that banner is the pattern the rest of docs/data should copy. (C) The MPM/porosity outputs (porosity_production_final, porosity_decomposition, porosity_regression_predictions, mpm_corner_realizability, mpm_coverage_plastic_vs_rigid, mpm_dpc_heckel_sweep, the four packing_dip_model files, particulate_se_size_sweep, percolation_2d_fit v1/v2) remain valid as records, but three of them are built on a target the 2026-08-12 platen correction and ledger CL-04/CL-07 have since qualified: they subtract MPM union porosity from DEM eps_sphere without converting and gate on that raw difference at 4 %p, when the measured convention offset is 1.251 %p. No quotation_ban value leaks anywhere in these 40 files - the numeric near-misses (an R_int of 52.0 Ohm.cm2 in kim2023, a porosity of 15.6 in porosity_decomposition) are unrelated quantities, and the ban registry's retracted sigma_e ratios appear nowhere. The two findings that actually cost something are provenance, not arithmetic: the "Minnmann pure-SE ~10 % @ 300 MPa" anchor is our own calibration convergence value wearing a literature label (audited and prescribed for relabel on 2026-06-26, never applied, now drafted into manuscript text), and sigma_grain = 3.0 mS/cm is still labelled "Cronau single-crystal" in this bucket's provenance file and in three code sites after the Cronau digest disowned that label. For v3: archive lhs_ext_design_20260829.csv and percolation_2d_fit.csv as history, collapse packing_dip_model.csv into its ps73 twin, and build one anchors index mapping each literature CSV to its paper and to the quantity it may anchor - that single index fixes the orphan family and would have caught both provenance leaks.

findings.claim: The repo's most-cited experimental compaction anchor - "pure-SE porosity ~10 % @ 300 MPa (Minnmann et al., LPSCl cold-press)" - does not exist in the file the repo itself designates as its provenance source, and a 2026-06-26 audit already concluded it is our own MPM calibration convergence value, not a Minnmann measurement. The label survives unchanged in CLAUDE.md, the pipeline guide and drafted manuscript text.

There is no pure-SE porosity row and no 300 MPa row anywhere in the file (its pure-SE rows carry only ionic conductivity 1.6 / 1.2 mS/cm). findings.claim: The production porosity table mixes two porosity conventions row by row - each row is either a DEM eps_sphere value or a scaffold-MPM union value, chosen by a raw 4 %p gate on their difference - while CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-12 correction measured that convention offset at 1.251 %p and instructs that all porosity be reported in eps_sphere. The gate therefore fires on a difference that already carries a systematic ~1.25 %p bias, and the published grid is convention-inhomogeneous.
findings.evidence: scripts/porosity_final_production.py lines 8-17: "gap = dem_eps_sphere - mpm_plastic; if gap > +4 ... use DEM; else use MPM (plastic)", GATE = 4.0; the output CSV's last column is literally `source` with values MPM / DEM(corner) (e.g. `0:10,0.0,70,0.0,2.0,0.5,50.7,13.1,2.4,MPM`). Contradicting source: CLAUDE.md, 512-grid section, correction dated 2026-08-12 - the 1.2 %p is not a constitutive-model difference but a bookkeeping offset, SE-SE 0.402 %p + AM-SE 0.848 %p = 1.251 %p, matching MPM-convention 16.877 minus eps_sphere 15.626 to three decimals, closing with "all porosity must be reported in eps_sphere". findings.proposed_action: Convert mpm_porosity_pct to eps_sphere before the gate. verdict: This bucket is two unrelated families that happen to sort together alphabetically. Family A (15 literature CSVs: reisacher, sangros x3, schneider, schreiner, shi, so x3, stomakhin, storakers, tailored, thakur, thorntonning, varkey, wet_processing, yun) is the healthiest data in the repo — every one carries a DOI, the material system, a stated-vs-digitized flag per row, and an explicit transferability caveat, and none touches a retracted number. They are canonical; leave them alone. Family B (16 run outputs plus the two real14 scaffolds and two presets) is the SR-01/SDCP/step3 measurement trail, and it is where the problems are. Its condition is best summarized by one number: of the 16 run outputs, exactly one (step3_transport_resolution_..._v3.json) satisfies the repo's own CL-75 rule that a measurement JSON must carry the commit SHA that made it — the rule written after a stale file of exactly this kind was cited as canon for three weeks. The rest carry no run identity, and three supersession conventions coexist: a self-labelling filename (sdcp_stamp_confound_rve_MOVINGCROP4.json, works), a retrofitted superseded_by block (step3 v2, works), and nothing at all (step3 v1, sr01_carbon_network.csv, sdcp8_v025/v03/v04.json — where the ledger's retractions fail to reach the data). One correction to the audit's premise, which matters for scoping the rest of the run: the ban sweep DOES read docs/data/*.json — BAN_SCAN_GLOBS at scripts/check_review_findings.py:104 includes 'docs/**/*.json' — but it has no *.csv pattern of any kind, leaving 134 CSVs under docs/ unswept. I ran all 22 registered quotation_ban patterns against all 38 files: zero hits, so carries_banned_value is false throughout. The real leak here is not a registered string but an unregistered instruction: sdcp_comparison_runs.csv tells its reader that vox 0.4 is the experimental anchor and belongs in the manuscript's main figure, which CL-24/CL-26/CL-41 all contradict, and no sweep can see it. For a v3 reorganization: keep Family A and wire the six missing card pointers; treat step3 v3 and sc_poly_preset.csv as the two schema templates and back-fill measure_provenance into the four SR-01 writers; archive sr01_raster_fix_impact.json (a dead one-off null result the ledger already quotes verbatim) and sdcp_prereg_v2_vox015_arms.json (a stale partial duplicate of prereg_v2/raw_sigma.json); mark or rename the three sdcp8_v0*.json files, the surviving artifacts of a sweep CL-31 invalidated wholesale and for which no replacement was ever run; and fix CLAUDE.md:44, where the top norm quotes a discredited estimator's numbers to assert the one sentence the live ledger says does not hold.

verdict: This is not a dead one-off sweep — it is the six-file audit package that closes findings.json R20-02, and it is the canonical evidence for a live ledger verdict (CL-48 = h1, the σ_VGCF single-fibre probe in which the SDCP gain reverses sign: SBE 6.525664 vs DBE 5.818477 S/cm, R = 0.891630, G = −0.1084, both arms converged at cg_info = 0 after --step3-maxiter 200000 beat the 785,400× phase contrast). All six files are live and machine-guarded: `check_cohort_packages.py` (via check_all.sh) audits the directory as "진단 패키지 (표지 ① 1 · ② 2팔) · cohort 판정 격리 확인", and I re-ran `sdcp_gain_verdict.py` on it — the committed verdict_receipt.txt reproduces line-for-line, i.e. the constraint "this arm may not be used for a production verdict" is enforced by the files themselves, not by prose. The package is also a genuinely well-formed comparison: its two arms share input_digest, input_files hashes and dof (26,438,766 / 26,796,346) exactly with the W4b baseline arms, so the 1.1265 → 0.8916 shift is a matched-bed measurement on the single registered axis σ_VGCF 78.5398 → 7854. carries_banned_value is false for all six (I scanned all 22 quotation_ban patterns against every file); note that docs/**/*.json IS inside BAN_SCAN_GLOBS, so the premise that JSON escapes the sweep does not hold in this repo — but .txt does escape, which is where verdict_receipt.txt sits. A v3 reorganization should keep this directory intact and unarchived — it is referenced evidence, not residue — and should fix four things around it rather than in it: the CL-48 ledger entry still claims the re-run was "the same problem" as the failed first attempt when the repo's own BED_DIGESTS registry says the two attempts sat on different bed generations (P1); CL-48 still says its raw data is not in the repo and carries no pointer to this path (P2); its "do not cite 6.53 / 5.82 S/cm" instruction is prose-only while comparable CL-33/CL-41 hold values are registered in quotation_ban (P2); and the only repo-sweep that guards the package's integrity does not run in CI (P3). The highest-value surfacing job is the σ_VGCF sensitivity axis — three measured ratio points now scattered across two cohorts and a ledger, one of which changes the sign of the paper's headline.

The h1 verdict itself is unaffected — the committed arms pair exactly with the W4b baseline (identical input_digest and identical dof 26,438,766 / 26,796,346), so R = 0.891630 vs 1.126481 is a matched-bed comparison. What is contradicted is the narrative continuity between attempt 1 and attempt 2, which invites reading 6.5468 → 6.5256 (−0.32 %) as a pure convergence error when the bed changed too.

verdict: This bucket is a single matched pair of 16-arm σ_e audit packages at vox 0.125 with the SDCP point stamp — a control (`sdcp_bridge_um` 0) and its treatment arm (`sdcp_bridge_um` 0.01) — both committed together in 673bdc664 (2026-08-30) as part of the "동반 cohort 9개 반입". Provenance is exemplary and nothing here is a quotation_ban leak: every file carries a reduction manifest with source sha256/byte counts, a tool commit, a sealed run receipt, and a frozen verdict receipt, and a sweep of all 22 registry patterns across all 38 files returns zero hits. These are scalar decision-audit packages, not raw data — the 130 MB field solutions were discarded, so they can never be re-solved, only re-scored, which the manifests say plainly. The control is a valid but deliberately non-quotable diagnostic: point stamp draws SDCP at 0.238× its true volume (CL-25/CL-33), so a_track_status_20260827.md §2 admits its ratio 1.009670 only as a "강도 프로브" with manuscript quotation forbidden. The treatment arm is not canonical and is not a null result — it is a void run. Its receipt records `sdcp_bridge_um: 0.01` next to `sdcp_stamp: point` / `sdcp_sphere_d_um: 0.0`, a combination that step3_sigma.py:449 now rejects outright precisely because the old guard `if sdcp_sphere_d_um and ...` skipped the entire bridge block, and all 16 of its arms are bit-identical to the control down to the last float. a_track_status_20260827.md §1 correctly calls this INVALID_TREATMENT_NOT_APPLIED and rules "판정하지 않는다"; three days later Table S3 §11-2 re-read the same bit-identity as a physical finding about single-cell points having nothing to connect — the exact leak pattern CLAUDE.md 작업 규율 ④ warns about, made possible because the invalidation was never entered in claims.json and because check_cohort_packages.py green-ticks both packages. Good news for the manuscript: the A-track number that actually reaches Methods ("recovers only about a fifth of that grid dependence", A = 0.197373) is computed from the four sphere-stamp cohorts, not from these, so no published figure is contaminated. For v3: keep the control as a labelled historical diagnostic; demote the treatment package to explicit void/provenance status rather than a ninth cohort, fix the "9/9" count and §11-2 in Table S3, and add the one-line receipt assertion that turns this from a prose memory into an enforced invariant — it flags both offenders (this one and the vox 0.15 twin in another bucket) for free.

findings.claim: docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §11-2 (dated 2026-08-30) reads this cohort pair as a physical result — "브리지는 점 스탬프에서 no-op 이다 (부수 소득) … ⇒ SDCP 에 공간적 크기가 있을 때만 브리지가 작동한다 — 한 셀짜리 점끼리는 이을 것이 없다" — and its §11 table lists the row `vox0125_b048_sbrg001_lean2_r2a31fc4a4437 | 0.125 | 점 | 0.01 | off | 52.93 | 53.45 | 1.009670` as a bridge-0.01 measurement. The bridge was in fact never applied, so no point-stamp bridge was ever measured and the stated mechanism is unverified (and only partly true even in principle).
findings.evidence: DATA: this run_receipt.json records `"sdcp_stamp": "point", "sdcp_sphere_d_um": 0.0, "sdcp_bridge_um": 0.01`, and all 16 arms are bit-identical to the control cohort (e.g. p2_DBE_a0 sigma_e_eff 0.053489840638594466 and n_dof 44538152 in BOTH dirs). CONTRADICTING SOURCE 1 — docs/reviews/a_track_status_20260827.md §1 (three days earlier): "1차 4런 판정 = INVALID_TREATMENT_NOT_APPLIED … 러너에 SDCP_SPHERE_D 를 안 넘겨 점 스탬프로 돌았고 … 앞 조건이 False 여서 아무 일도 안 했다 … 효과 0 = fail-open … 처치가 가해지지 않았으므로 그 h0 은 가짜다. 판정하지 않는다." CONTRADICTING SOURCE 2 — scripts/step3_sigma.py:449 now hard-rejects the combination: `if float(sdcp_bridge_um) > 0.0 and not sdcp_sphere_d_um: raise ValueError(... "under the point stamp it would be a silent no-op" ... [fail-closed guard added 2026-08-27 after the A-track treatment arms came out bit-identical to their controls])`. CONTRADICTING SOURCE 3 — the doc's mechanism covers only one of three bridge branches: at step3_sigma.py:465-482 branch ⓐ (SDCP–SDCP) does collapse at r_s=0, but branch ⓑ (SDCP–AM, `_d <= _rs + am_r[_a] + _tol`) and branch ⓒ (SDCP–VGCF) do not require SDCP spatial extent to be non-degenerate, so "nothing to connect" does not follow; the guard skipped all three branches.
findings.proposed_action: Add an INVALID_TREATMENT_NOT_APPLIED banner to the two point-stamp `sbrg001` rows of docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §11, and either delete §11-2 or restate it as "the treatment arm was void (fail-open, a_track_status_20260827.md §1); the bit-identity is a code-path artifact, not a measurement of a point-stamp bridge". Drop the mechanism sentence "한 셀짜리 점끼리는 이을 것이 없다". Register the invalidation as a CL entry so it outranks prose.

findings.claim: This entire 19-file package is a scientific duplicate of docs/data/cohorts/prereg_v2_vox0125_b048_lean2_r9cb46e88f35d_reduced — all 16 arms agree to full float precision in sigma_e_eff_S_cm and exactly in n_dof, and verdict_receipt.txt is byte-identical. findings.claim: The invalidation of these runs lives only in prose. docs/reviews/claims.json — the canonical ledger that outranks prose per CLAUDE.md — has zero occurrences of `INVALID_TREATMENT_NOT_APPLIED`, `1.009670` or any A-track entry, and scripts/check_cohort_packages.py (run by scripts/check_all.sh and the pre-commit gate) green-ticks both packages. Running `python3 scripts/check_cohort_packages.py` prints `✓ prereg_v2_vox0125_b048_sbrg001_lean2_r2a31fc4a4437_reduced  비 1.009670 (원장 일치)` with no warning. CLAUDE.md 작업 규율 ④ names this failure mode: "정본은 밖으로 강제되지 않으면 새어나간다".

surface_worthy.why: The point stamp and the sphere stamp move in OPPOSITE directions as the grid is refined, and that sign contrast is direct support for CL-25's representation-volume mechanism — yet it is not stated anywhere as a single fact. It has to be assembled by hand from a_track_status_20260827.md §2 and the Table S3 §11 table. It is the same class as the `--fibre` silent-stamp regression that CLAUDE.md 규칙 F was created for, but unlike that one it has surviving committed evidence anyone can re-derive. verdict: This bucket is 38 of the ~57 files making up three of the ten `docs/data/cohorts/` packages: scalar decision-audit reductions (schema `reduced-arm/2`, ~5.8 kB per arm, produced by `scripts/reduce_arm_payloads.py` from ~131 MB GPU payloads that were never committed) of three 16-arm origin-factorial σ_e cohorts at vox 0.125 on the 2026-08-27 regenerated SBE/DBE bed pair — (D1) SDCP sphere-stamp Ø0.30, PTFE off, ratio 1.143327; (D2) same plus PTFE centerline, ratio 1.335498; (D3) same plus sdcp_bridge 0.01 µm, ratio 1.343368 (only its manifest is in this bucket). All three are p2 plate rule (`p2-occupied-surface-first`), LEAN=2 (σ_e only — `--no-ion --no-pore --no-collector --no-thermal`), 8/8 arms converged (`cg_info 0`, resid ~1e-8), and every value I recomputed from the arms reproduces `docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md` §11/§17 to six decimals. This is the canonical and only copy — nothing duplicates it, the originals are gone, and the src_sha256 chain is the sole link back to them. It is live, not archivable: `scripts/check_cohort_packages.py` reads the arms on every `check_all.sh` run, and these three cohorts are three of the eight cells of the §17 2×2×2 PTFE × grid × bridge factorial. Ban sweep: I checked all 22 `quotation_ban` patterns against all 57 bytes-on-disk files — zero hits, and the two near-miss numbers (D1's p2 1.143327 vs CL-41's banned p1 1.143817; §17's p2 1.123672 vs CL-33's banned p1 1.123191) are genuinely distinct measurements, so `carries_banned_value` is false throughout. What a v3 reorganization must not do is flatten this into "one more sweep directory": the six findings above are all reader-facing rather than data-facing — the ledger's newest entry (CL-86) says one of these numbers is unverified when the repo verifies it on demand, the checker that does that verification is missing from CI, three of the four PTFE contrasts fail the repo's own `--compare-dir` gate on `code_sha` (benignly — the solver files are byte-identical across c2f5b047→d45576e2 — but undisclosed), one package was reduced from a dirty tree with no gate to notice, and two frozen receipts use an "표준오차" label the repo has since retracted. The right v3 move is a short README at `docs/data/cohorts/` carrying the bed generation, the plate-rule generation, the code_sha map across cells, the R8-Q1 spread wording, and the one command that regenerates every number — plus wiring `check_cohort_packages.py` into `discipline.yml` so the package↔ledger agreement stops depending on someone remembering.

Same HOLD for r668c420eb7db↔r8ef120e36b33 and r2f46127f44a8↔rd2be19ea80e4. verdict: This bucket is one coherent family: three "reduced-arm/2" audit packages from the prereg-v2 SDCP electronic-gain campaign, each a complete 16-arm {0,1/2}^3 origin factorial (8 SBE + 8 DBE) reduced from ~131 MB solver payloads to ~6 kB of scalars by scripts/reduce_arm_payloads.py, plus their runner receipts and frozen verdict printouts. My 38 paths cover the vox 0.125 sphere-stamp pair that differs only in the PTFE axis (r8ef120e36b33 = PTFE centerline, ratio 1.343368; r668c420eb7db = PTFE off, ratio 1.149268) and the manifest of the vox 0.15 point-stamp cohort (red940fcbfd13, ratio 1.016076). These are NOT a dead one-off sweep and must not be archived: all three are p2-plate-rule ("p2-occupied-surface-first") measurements, i.e. the re-measurement CL-41 demanded after the p1 values were quotation-banned, and they are actively enforced - scripts/check_cohort_packages.py recomputes every ratio from the arms' sigma_e_eff_S_cm and fails if it disagrees with docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md, and scripts/check_all.sh runs it. I verified the packages independently: all 48 arm files hash-match their manifests byte-for-byte, all three run_receipts hash-match manifest.receipt_sha256, my recomputed paired ratios reproduce the ledger to six digits (1.343368 / 1.149268 / 1.016076), and none of the 38 files contains any of the 22 registered quotation_ban patterns - so carries_banned_value is false throughout and there is no ban leak here. Two of the three are load-bearing for live conclusions (the A-track h0 A = 0.197373 and the §17 PTFE main effect); the vox 0.15 point-stamp package is a deliberately labelled intensity probe whose value is quotation-restricted by CL-33 for a different reason (SDCP represented volume 0.238x true). What v3 should do: keep all three verbatim as the canonical p2 audit layer, give docs/data/cohorts/ a README mapping each package to its axes, ratio and ledger section, add a CLAUDE.md pointer (the top norm currently contains zero occurrences of "cohort" or "table_s3", so this entire evidence layer is invisible from the document every session loads), and fix three provenance defects the current checker cannot see - the A2 manifest's "+dirty" tool_commit that disagrees with its own arms, the unresolvable code_sha f286ac74 behind the point-stamp packages, and the pre-R8-Q1 receipts that still call the origin-phase spread a standard error.

The other two cohorts in this bucket are self-consistent (both halves `d45576e2a5261...`, no `+dirty`), and docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:586 records `+dirty 없음` as a package quality criterion. findings.claim: The receipts' headline `σ_e 비` is computed with the non-canonical mean-of-means estimator, so the number a reader takes off the top line differs from the registered (paired) estimator that the ledger and the CI checker use.

I recomputed both estimators from the 16 arm payloads: mean(DBE)/mean(SBE) = 1.343307 and 1.149280; paired-mean = 1.343368 and 1.149268. Contradicting source: scripts/check_cohort_packages.py docstring - "⚠ estimator 는 쌍대응 비의 산술평균이다 (개정 A1 등록). `mean(DBE)/mean(SBE)` 는 정본이 아니다 - 둘은 6자리에서 갈린다" - and docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §17/§11 which record 1.343368 and 1.149268. The registered analysis form is docs/reviews/sdcp_bridge_prereg_amendment_A1_20260827.md (§0-§1 still valid).
findings.proposed_action: Swap the print order in sdcp_gain_verdict.py so the registered paired mean is the headline and mean/mean is the annotated auxiliary, and note in table_s3 §11/§17 that committed receipts predate that change. No verdict flips - the divergence is at the 5th decimal and both sit far from the h0/h1 thresholds.

findings.claim: This package seals a run whose code_sha does not exist anywhere in this repository, while its sibling cohorts' code_sha do resolve - and nothing in the checker or the ledger distinguishes the two cases.
findings.evidence: The manifest's receipt_sha256 (2674b6127c04a212...) hash-matches run_receipt.json, which declares `"code_sha": "f286ac74"`. `git rev-parse f286ac74` and `git log -1 f286ac74` both fail with `unknown revision`, and `git log --all` finds no such commit. By contrast the other two cohorts in this bucket resolve cleanly: c2f5b047 = 2026-08-27 "step3: stop the require-gpu selftest from depending on the absence of a GPU" and d45576e2 = 2026-08-29 "Add a runner axis for the ionic solve...", both ancestors of HEAD. All four point-stamp cohorts in docs/data/cohorts/ share the unresolvable f286ac74; all six sphere-stamp cohorts resolve. docs/reviews/a_track_status_20260827.md §3 explains that runs execute from a different working repo (`~/dem-mt`), which makes the asymmetry - not the absence itself - the defect: a reader cannot tell which packages are code-reproducible from this branch.
findings.proposed_action: Have check_cohort_packages.py test `git cat-file -e <code_sha>` per package and report `code not in this repo` rather than passing silently, and mark the four point-stamp cohorts in table_s3 §11 as sealed against an out-of-repo commit. Longer term the run receipt should record the producing repo/remote alongside the sha.

findings.claim: The ledger's PTFE main effect is differenced across a code_sha boundary that the ledger does not record. I verified it is harmless on this path, but the verification is nowhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: code_sha aliases perfectly with the PTFE axis across all ten committed cohorts: every `ptfe_stamp: centerline` run is d45576e2, every sphere-stamp `ptfe_stamp: off` run is c2f5b047, every point-stamp run is f286ac74. docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §17-2 reports the PTFE effect as `+0.189307, 범위 +0.184148 … +0.194100`, and its largest cell, +0.194100, is exactly 1.343368 (this receipt's cohort, d45576e2) minus 1.149268 (r668c420eb7db, c2f5b047). The ledger flags the vox axis as a composite axis at §17-2b but says nothing about code version. CLAUDE.md's `--compare-dir --expect-differ` contract requires `등록 밖 인자 불변`. I settled it by measurement: `git diff --stat c2f5b047 d45576e2` touches only bridge_grid_verdict.py, check_all.sh, check_review_findings.py, reduce_arm_payloads.py and docs, plus a purely additive LEAN=3 branch in scripts/sdcp_gain_vox015_8arm.sh; step3_sigma.py and the solver are untouched and the LEAN=2 flag string is unchanged, so the sigma_e path these cohorts ran is bit-identical between the two commits.
findings.proposed_action: Add one line to table_s3 §17-2 recording that the PTFE axis is aliased with code_sha (d45576e2 vs c2f5b047) and that the alias is verified inert for LEAN=2 sigma_e, with the diff as evidence - otherwise the next reviewer re-derives this or, worse, treats it as a live confound.

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md - the top norm - contains zero pointers to docs/data/cohorts/ or to the ledger that governs it, so this whole p2 evidence layer is unreachable from the document every session loads.
findings.evidence: `grep -c cohort CLAUDE.md` = 0 and `grep -c table_s3 CLAUDE.md` = 0, while ten sealed cohorts sit in docs/data/cohorts/, scripts/check_all.sh:135 runs check_cohort_packages.py against them, and docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §11/§17 is the ledger prose that checker enforces. Meanwhile CLAUDE.md's SR-01 section still narrates only the p1 grid sweep, lists its three values as quotation-banned, and says the citable form is available only `p2 재측정 후` - even though p2 sphere-stamp measurements at vox 0.15 and 0.125 now exist in this directory (1.123672 / 1.143327 bridge-off, 1.133492 / 1.149268 bridge-on), and this very cohort supplies the bridge-on grid contrast u = +0.015776 behind the live A-track verdict A = 0.197373 (table_s3 §11-1). There is also no README or index in docs/data/cohorts/.
findings.proposed_action: In v3, give docs/data/cohorts/ a README that names each package, its axes, its ratio and its ledger section, and add a single SR-01 line in CLAUDE.md pointing at table_s3_data_20260827.md §11/§17 as the p2 evidence layer. This is exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule ④ describes - canon that is not enforced outward leaks.

findings.claim: This cohort has a near-twin whose 16 arms are numerically identical, and their verdict receipts are byte-identical - because the receipt does not name its own run. The duplication is intentional (a negative control) but the receipt cannot be attributed once separated from its directory.
findings.evidence: Comparing this package against docs/data/cohorts/prereg_v2_vox015_b048_sbrg001_lean2_r8da7764bead7_reduced: all 16 arms have identical sigma_e_eff_S_cm and identical n_dof; only physics_protocol_id (p2-5016275b5b26f4ad vs p2-47723e6f74cf53fb) and the requested sdcp_bridge_um (0.0 vs 0.01) differ; and the two verdict_receipt.txt files are byte-identical (sha256 equal). The receipt's only provenance line is `# sdcp_gain_verdict.py --dir <원본>` - the directory is elided. The duplication itself is documented and load-bearing: table_s3 §11-2 uses exactly this pair to show the bridge is a no-op at point stamp and that the convention hash records settings rather than answers.
findings.proposed_action: Keep both packages - they are the evidence for §11-2, not redundancy to archive. Have sdcp_gain_verdict.py write the source directory and receipt_digest into the receipt header so a receipt is self-identifying.

surface_worthy.why: The reduction ratio is the reason this evidence layer is commitable at all, and it is the template any v3 data-hub design should copy for other tracks (STEP4, Phase A) rather than re-invent.

verdict: This bucket is three committed "reduced-arm/2" decision-audit packages from the SDCP electronic-gain track: two vox-0.15 point-stamp cohorts (bridge off / bridge on) and the manifest of the vox-0.15 sphere-stamp + PTFE-centerline cohort. They are scalar packages by design — the manifests say so ("solver/viz 재생용 원자료가 아니다") — each ~5 kB reduction of a ~130 MB payload, 16 arms per cohort (SBE/DBE x 8 half-cell origin shifts), all cg_info 0. Integrity is perfect: I verified every out_sha256 and out_bytes against disk and every receipt_sha256 against its run_receipt.json, and independently recomputed the paired ratios (1.016076 for both point cohorts, 1.320301 for the sphere cell) to the digit against the ledger table in docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §11. No banned value appears anywhere: I ran all 22 quotation_ban patterns over all 38 files and got zero hits, which is expected because these are the p2-plate-rule re-measurements that CLAUDE.md says must exist before the retracted p1 numbers can be replaced — the arm manifests all record plate_rule "p2-occupied-surface-first". The 37 JSONs are inside the ban sweep's globs (docs/**/*.json), contrary to the assumption in the audit brief; the two .txt files are not. verdict: This is not a dead one-off sweep — it is two cells of the repo's canonical σ_e convention factorial, and both are load-bearing today. Each directory is a 16-arm complete {0, vox/2}³ origin factorial at vox 0.15, sphere SDCP stamp Ø0.30, sdcp_bridge 0.01, reduced by scripts/reduce_arm_payloads.py from ~131 MB per arm to 5.8 kB scalar audit payloads. r2f46127f44a8 is the PTFE-off cell (paired-origin ratio 1.133492); rd2be19ea80e4 is the PTFE-centerline cell (1.320301). Provenance is unusually complete for this repo: every arm carries input_digest (04b5a565ff4069f4 = SBE, d1022e090ab625a9 = DBE, both registered), code_sha, physics_protocol_id, plate_rule, the full σ table and every stamp axis; the run_receipt seals the runner's intent; the cohort_manifest holds src_sha256 for all 16 originals; 16/16 arms converged (cg_info 0). I re-ran the repo's own checkers read-only: scripts/check_cohort_packages.py recomputes both ratios from the arms and matches the ledger, and scripts/bridge_grid_verdict.py reproduces the A-track statistic A = 0.197373 exactly from r2f46127f44a8 plus three sibling packages. Canonicity: these are the SDCP-contact-bridge-on variants of the manuscript's nominal W4/W4b cohorts, so they are NOT the headline numbers — table_s3 §11 says so explicitly ("이것은 헤드라인이 아니다 … 측정 기록"). They are the second arm of a registered contrast, and they are current, not superseded: they use the corrected p2-occupied-surface-first plate rule (so they are the replacement for, not an instance of, the quotation-banned p1 sphere-stamp family), the newer 2026-08-27 regenerated bed with ADD_E_SET additive moduli, and no finer bridge-on run at vox 0.15 exists. Ban check: running all 22 quotation_ban patterns over all 37 files gives zero hits; carries_banned_value is false throughout. For the v3 reorganization: keep both directories intact and co-located with their bridge-0 twins (w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827, w4b_ptfe_off_20260827), which currently sit one directory level away under docs/data/ and break the factorial's discoverability; nothing here is archivable. Two things need action rather than storage — the A2-registered centerline A-track verdict was measured but never written down (A = 0.166576, h0), and CLAUDE.md still carries the n=1 arm-0 pair plus its retracted bracket argument for exactly the contrast these packages measured with eight arms. verdict: This is not a dead one-off sweep. The 10 files are one physical bed of the real_14 design captured in five states — loose (LIGGGHTS step 405000, platen not yet in contact) and compacted at 100/200/300/600 MPa — in LIGGGHTS box units as `type,x,y,z,r`, 31,834–31,885 particles each (36 AM_P r=6 µm, ~400 AM_S r=2 µm, ~31,400 SE r=0.5 µm). Provenance is closed and self-consistent: each header's plate_z equals the corresponding thickness_um and each AM+SE total equals the N_particles column of docs/data/heckel_real14_composite_multiP.csv, which is the ledger behind the four-point Heckel fit (P_y 133 MPa) and the four measured f_AM values that the live ledger entry CDX-19 keeps. Geometry checks clean: no duplicate positions, correct radii, monotone descent of the top surface with pressure, particles overhanging plate_z by only 0.25–1.0 µm (softened-contact overlap). Nothing here carries a quotation_ban value — the registry's patterns are σ ratios and percentages, and the only literal hits ('35.79', '0.147') are substrings of coordinates, which no reader or plot would take as a current claim; the CSVs contain no derived quantities at all. These are canonical: they are the sole copy, they are the only multi-pressure particle-coordinate record in the repo (real14_*_scaffold.csv is a different realization — 457 AM, 30.28 µm at 300 MPa), and two live runner scripts plus fifteen committed MPM result JSONs depend on them. A v3 reorganization should keep all ten together, register the directory in the data inventory (which today asserts real14 is the only coordinate-bearing scaffold — the one factual error found here), and carry three labels alongside them: P200 is an unconsumed input for a preregistered sweep that its own judge still reports INCOMPLETE; the P100/P300/P600 pair is wired into a runner whose configuration the canonical doc declared void for circularity; and LOOSE is the corrective bed whose three runs were executed, disagree with DEM by up to +29.7 %, and have never been written down anywhere.

verdict:
This is a complete, well-formed 8-arm GPU cohort - scenario 1 (r = sigma_ion(SDCP)/sigma_ion(SE) = 0) of the four-scenario ionic origin ensemble registered in docs/reviews/ion_8arm_prereg_20260831.md, itself the 8-arm re-run of ion_r_sensitivity_prereg_20260831.md (STEP B). Sixteen reduced payloads (8 origin phases x SBE/DBE, 131 MB each stripped to ~9 kB of scalars), a run receipt, a reduction manifest with per-arm src_sha256, and a captured verdict stdout. Provenance is unusually good for this repo: code_sha 657c2192 resolves in git, receipt_digest 9b7907b3fdc4 matches the source directory name, all 16 arms converged (cg_info 0, no unconverged flags), the origins are the exact {0, 0.075}^3 factorial the receipt declares, and every non-registered manifest axis - 21 of them, including dilate_z and plate_rule, the two that CLAUDE.md rule (5) says used to escape cross-directory checks - matches the canonical w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827 package exactly. Every number the canon reports from this cohort reproduces from the raw files to the last digit I checked: paired sigma_e ratio 1.307820 with origin spread 0.002977 and means 53.99 / 70.61 mS/cm, paired sigma_ion ratio 0.977642 with SD 0.000090 and ranges 0.5503-0.5534 / 0.5380-0.5410 mS/cm. It carries no retracted value: I ran all 22 quotation_ban patterns over all 19 files and got zero hits, and the sweep does cover this directory (BAN_SCAN_GLOBS includes docs/**/*.json) - the brief's premise that the sweep ignores JSON is wrong for this repo; only the .txt receipt is outside it. The ratio it does carry, 1.307820, is a p2-occupied-surface-first result and is therefore the re-measurement the p1 ban (R5-CX-06) was waiting for, not a leak.

It remains the canonical copy of exactly one thing: the r = 0 ionic measurement. Its electronic half is the fifth bit-identical copy of a single measurement and should be labelled as such in v3, not archived - table_s3 §20-2 and §21-1 treat that bit-identity as a deliberate like-for-like regression result, and destroying the copies would destroy the evidence. What v3 should fix is the pointer, not the data: scripts/plot_sigma_e_bars.py defaults --dir to this ionic cohort, so the manuscript's sigma_e bar figure and docs/figures/sigma_e_bars.csv are generated from the r=0 package rather than from the electronic canon, and that CSV carries no provenance header at all. Two live corrections are owed against this family, both from canon that postdates the cohort: CL-59's verdict still asks for an r = 0 arm that these files are, and CL-81 (2026-09-08, the newest ionic ruling) requires a CONTACT_FREE upper-bound label wherever these absolute sigma_ion values sit beside experiment - which they do, in ms_si_v7 §3-3, with the 4x gap attributed entirely to the reference sigma_SE. And the package's own verdict_receipt.txt renders a bold h0 for the electronic test it was forbidden to re-decide, while omitting the ionic ratio it was built to produce; the correction exists in table_s3 §20-4 but nothing inside the directory says so. Two lines of README next to these files would close most of that.

verdict: This is not a dead one-off sweep — it is a live, canonical, and unusually well-provenanced measurement package, and it should survive the v3 reorganization essentially intact. All 19 files are the committed audit package for one scenario of the four-point σ_ion(SDCP) sweep registered by docs/reviews/ion_8arm_prereg_20260831.md and adjudicated in docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §21: 8 SBE + 8 DBE arms at vox 0.15, sphere SDCP stamp (Ø0.30), PTFE centerline, on the 2026-08-27 W2 beds, at the full {0, vox/2}³ origin factorial. This bucket is the r = 1/3 point (σ_ion(SDCP) = 1.0e-3, the prereg's 'historically uncorrected solver default'). Provenance checks all pass: 16/16 payload out_sha256 and out_bytes reproduce, the manifest's receipt_sha256 matches run_receipt.json, code_sha 657c2192 and tool_commit 4d399afc2 both resolve to real commits, all 16 arms converged (cg_info 0, resid ~1e-8), one physics_protocol_id across the package, and a manifest diff shows SBE and DBE differ only in the registered contrast (bed inputs, additive set, PTFE cell count) — dilate_z, plate_rule, periodic_xy and every σ table are identical, so none of the rule-M hidden-axis leakage applies. scripts/check_all.sh runs scripts/check_cohort_packages.py against it on every push and it passes. No quotation_ban pattern appears in any file (I swept all 22 patterns over all 19 files); the ratios here (1.307820 σ_e, 1.008290 σ_ion) are the canon's own live p2-convention values, not the banned p1 family, though they sit one digit from banned neighbours and a writer should check the registry before typing any four-digit ratio. What the reorganization should do with it: keep all four ion8_* directories as the σ_ion sweep (they are the only real-bed voxel ionic data the repo has), give them a single findable hub entry instead of a §21 buried in a 1,500-line ledger, and treat docs/data/w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827/ as archivable — this bucket reproduces its electronic half bit-for-bit under a later code_sha and adds σ_ion. The one thing that must be fixed before anything ships is the P0: the SI edit sheet prints these σ_ion absolutes beside an experimental EIS value with the sole-cause attribution that CL-81 forbids, and the mandated CONTACT_FREE upper-bound label is absent from the manuscript path entirely.

verdict: This is one complete, well-formed measurement cohort, not a scatter of leftovers: scenario 3 of 4 of the ion 8-arm sweep registered in docs/reviews/ion_8arm_prereg_20260831.md, run 2026-08-31, committed as 4d399afc2. Sixteen reduced STEP3 payloads (8 origins x {SBE, DBE}, a complete {0, vox/2}^3 factorial) at vox 0.15 um, SDCP sphere Ø0.30, PTFE centerline, plate_rule p2-occupied-surface-first, protocol p2-4607dfa2d9bca9c7, code_sha 657c2192, beds SBE 04b5a565ff4069f4 / DBE d1022e090ab625a9 (the same W2 pair as w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827), with the one swept axis sigma_ion_sdcp = 5.21007e-04 S/cm (r = 0.1737, the RSA/D13 inversion) against sigma_ion_se = 0.003. Provenance is exemplary and I verified it rather than trusting it: all 16 out_sha256 and out_bytes match cohort_manifest.json, run_receipt.json's own sha256 equals the manifest's receipt_sha256, receipt_digest c915ac33c06e is the tail of source_dir, and all 16 arms converged (cg_info 0, ion_cg_info 0, resid <= 1.0e-08). Recomputing from the payloads reproduces docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md §21-2's row exactly — paired R̄ 0.997227, origin SD 0.000080, |R̄−1|/SD = 35, SBE 0.5503–0.5534 and DBE 0.5487–0.5518 mS/cm — so the doc that cites this bucket is accurate and this bucket is still its canonical source. Nothing here carries a banned value: I scanned all 19 files against all 22 quotation_ban patterns including whitespace-stripped numeric cores and got zero hits, which is expected because the ban registry targets p1-plate-rule and vox-0.4 values while this is p2 throughout. Status: live, but with a sharply limited live surface. Only the 8 DBE arms hold anything unique — the 8 SBE arms are bit-identical to the SBE arms of all three sibling cohorts, and all 16 sigma_e values are bit-identical to w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827, giving five stored copies of one electronic solve (deliberate, and used as load-bearing regression evidence in §20-2 and §21-1, so do not dedupe it silently). What a v3 reorganization should do: keep the directory intact and archive-label it rather than delete it, because CL-59 (live) declares "D13 · 8팔 이온 런은 원고에 불필요해졌다" while table_s3 §21-3 shows the run nonetheless closed the prereg and lifted the citation gate — it is a finished, adjudicated, manuscript-superfluous sweep, which is precisely the "safe to archive, unsafe to discard" category. Three things must travel with it: (1) the ledger has no CL entry for this run at all, so the verdict lives only in prose and CL-59 still claims the ionic origin dispersion is unmeasured and the r=0 arm missing, both of which this family disproves; (2) the shipped verdict_receipt.txt adjudicates the electronic axis under a different prereg's thresholds, which the registration explicitly forbade re-testing, and is byte-identical across all four cohorts, so the receipt cannot distinguish them; (3) the newest ledger entry, CL-81, places all voxel sigma_ion on the CONTACT_FREE branch with a bed-structure-dependent 6x spread and forbids unbacked common-mode arguments, which bites directly on the 0.28 % direction statement §21-3 licenses from these arms. Add a one-line README naming the swept axis, the canonical electronic sibling, and the CONTACT_FREE label, and extend check_cohort_packages.py to guard sigma_ion — right now the only automated check over this directory guards the one axis that is a duplicate of somewhere else.

verdict: This is a complete, well-provenanced measurement package and it is NOT a dead one-off: it is scenario 2 of 4 in the ion 8-arm origin ensemble registered by docs/reviews/ion_8arm_prereg_20260831.md — 8 SBE + 8 DBE arms at the full {0, vox/2}³ origin factorial, vox 0.15, SDCP sphere-stamped at Ø0.30 µm, PTFE centerline, bridge 0.48, plate rule p2-occupied-surface-first, LEAN=3 (σ_e and σ_ion both solved, 16/16 converged, cg_info = ion_cg_info = 0), on the 2026-08-27 W2 beds (ADD_E_SET_20260818: PTFE 1.8 / SDCP 9.0 GPa, so the CL-56 old-anchor caveat does not apply) with SBE and DBE sharing scaffold SHA 6184147f573f021d. Its axis is σ_ion(SDCP) = 5.5216e-05 S/cm, the Maxwell–Garnett point r = 0.0184 carried into the production σ_SE = 3.0e-3 convention. It is canonical for that axis and nothing supersedes it — the four cohorts are the current, cited generation, and this one is the only committed 8-origin measurement of the MG scenario. I re-derived its headline numbers from the payloads and they reproduce the ledger prose exactly: paired R_ion = 0.980371 with origin SD 8.73e-05 (table_s3 §21-2: 0.980371, 0.000087), σ_ion SBE 0.5503–0.5534 / DBE 0.5395–0.5425 mS/cm, paired R_e = 1.307820 (check_cohort_packages passes it green against the ledger), and the arm-0 pair confirms CL-59's derived linear-FV conversion to five figures. Zero quotation_ban leaks: I ran all 22 registered patterns against all 19 files and got 0 hits, and 18 of 19 are inside BAN_SCAN_GLOBS anyway via docs/**/*.json (only verdict_receipt.txt, a .txt, is unswept). What is wrong here is not the data but its accounting. Three things are load-bearing: the shipped verdict_receipt.txt prints a hypothesis verdict from a different preregistration with no disclaimer, and that disclaimer exists only in a review document (P1); the ionic ratio the package exists to produce has no machine check anywhere — the registered decider ion_r_verdict.py refuses the cohort outright because it is pinned to arm 0 and to the σ_SE = 0.00357 scenario set, while check_cohort_packages re-derives only σ_e (P1); and claims.json, which CANON says outranks prose, still records the ionic origin spread as unmeasured and origin generalization as HOLD in CL-59, with no ledger entry for the 8-arm campaign at all, so the strongest ionic result in the repo lives only in §21 of a 1517-line review file (P1). A v3 reorganization should keep all 19 files exactly as they are, add the missing claims.json entry, extend the two checkers to cover the ionic axis, and give docs/data/ion8_* a README that maps the four lossy directory names to their real σ_ion(SDCP) values, names the canonical source for the five-fold-duplicated centerline σ_e, and surfaces the ion_dissipation_share and CONTACT_FREE-labelled σ_ion absolutes that are currently invisible.

The duplication is intentional and documented as like-for-like regression evidence (table_s3 §20-2, §21-1: 'σ_e 가 `w4` 와 **64/64 팔 비트 동일**'), and ion_8arm_prereg §6 accepted the cost ('SBE 는 `r` 무관인데 시나리오마다 다시 푼다 (24팔 ≈ 10 h 낭비)'). What is missing is the canonical marker: scripts/plot_sigma_e_bars.py:91 hardcodes `--dir` default docs/data/ion8_isd0_20260831, an arbitrary pick among the five.
findings.proposed_action: Keep all five (the bit-identity IS the regression evidence). In the v3 reorg, add a one-line docs/data/ion8_*/README.md naming w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827 as the canonical σ_e centerline source and the four ion8_* dirs as canonical only for their own σ_ion axis, and point plot_sigma_e_bars.py's default at the canonical one.

findings.claim: The directory name misstates its own parameter by four orders of magnitude — 'isd55216e-05' parses as 5.5216e-01, while every manifest inside declares 5.5216e-05 — because the runner's tag rule deletes the decimal point.
findings.evidence: All 16 payloads carry step3.manifest.sigma_ion_sdcp_S_cm = 5.5216e-05 and run_receipt.json carries sigma_ion_sdcp_S_cm 5.5216e-05, while the directory reads 'isd55216e-05'. findings.json SELF-16 records the mechanism ('러너의 태그 규칙은 `${VAR//./}` = 점을 지운다') and notes the lossless `.`→`p` fix was applied only to two other axes, so the isd axis still strips. The same defect on the sibling docs/data/ion8_isd10e-03_20260831 is already logged P1 by docs/data/audit_20260909/audit1_scopes.json [22]/findings[18]; this is the identical defect on the same axis, and the correct mapping exists only in ion_8arm_prereg_20260831.md §2-1 and table_s3 §21-2.
findings.proposed_action: Do not rename the committed directories (the names are cited in three review docs and in plot_sigma_e_bars.py). Extend the runner's `.`→`p` substitution to the isd axis for future runs, and record the four name→value mappings in the docs/data/ion8_* README proposed above.

surface_worthy.why: Every payload carries step3.ion_dissipation_share, and across the four ion8 cohorts it gives the ionic conduction share carried by SDCP over the whole registered r-span — the exact quantity docs/reviews/fable_review_doping_20260819.md says must be computed before the doping prereg's threshold can be set ('s = 대조팔 ion_dissipation_share 로 런 전 산출'). It has never been extracted. It also supplies a second, independent negative control the current verdict does not use: the SBE arms report SDCP share 0.0000 in all 32 arms, as they must, since SBE has no SDCP.
surface_worthy.one_line: SDCP's share of ionic dissipation, DBE, 8/8 arms: 0.0000 (r=0) → 0.0027 (r=0.0184, this cohort) → 0.0146 (r=0.174) → 0.0190 (r=0.333); SBE 0.0000 throughout.

surface_worthy.one_line: DBE electronic dissipation share: VGCF 0.8792 · AM_S 0.1134 · SDCP 0.0074 · SE/PTFE 0 (SBE: VGCF 0.8672 · AM_S 0.1328).

verdict: This is not a dead one-off sweep — it is live, load-bearing measurement infrastructure and should be kept and promoted in v3, not archived. The 35 files are the five P:S-controlled electrode beds (kit_ps_{0_10,3_7,5_5,7_3,10_0}, LIGGGHTS cases 260421_2149-2154) rescued from the V100 before it was returned (commit 986fa7bcb, 2026-08-07), plus fracture scaffolds and per-kit runners added by commit 466926c53 (2026-08-11) and retro-patched by 4c751ed65. All 15 gzip members pass integrity, and I confirmed the bucket is still the canonical copy by recomputing the canon's own geometry columns from the raw scaffolds: SE/solid, S_AM and d_h for all five beds match docs/se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md to the printed digit, and V_SE for ps_7_3 matches its line 66 exactly. Downstream, kit_ps_7_3 is the default bed for three live tools — sr01_realbed_ab.py (SR-01 raster A/B, ledger CL-15), step3_transport_resolution.py (grid ledger, CL-25/CL-75) and step4_angular_risk.py (CL-76) — and kit_ps_7_3__run_mpm.sh is a selftest fixture in sr01_stamp_compare.py, so deleting or renaming anything here breaks running code. Zero quotation_ban leaks: I ran all 22 registry patterns over every decompressed member and got 0 hits (worth noting for the audit's own framing — docs/**/*.json IS inside BAN_SCAN_GLOBS, so the manifests are swept; the .csv.gz payloads and, more importantly, the ten .sh runners are not). What a v3 reorganization should do: (1) fix the P1 first — the canon doc's two headline tables still carry the ps_7_3 sigma value that the same doc disowns 400 lines later, which is the discipline-4 propagation failure in miniature; (2) reunite the sixth bed, real14, with its five siblings or document why it is stored differently, since the commit message claims it is here and it is not; (3) collapse the eight byte-identical runner copies and strike the false 'all hashes differ' rationale that justifies them; (4) surface the fracture scaffolds, which contain a clean, never-tabulated result (bimodal packing shields AM from fracture; both mono endpoints fail badly in opposite ways) that answers an open CLAUDE.md validation target.

findings.claim: The live canon doc for the d_h track still prints the superseded, self-disowned value sigma(kit_ps_7_3, phi=0.72) = 0.4671 in both of its headline tables, and derives the quoted 192-grid collapse exponent from it — while the same document 400 lines later records the measured replacement 0.4226 and CLAUDE.md's canon 192 5-bed citation is -0.563 / R2 0.910.
findings.evidence: Data side: kit_ps_7_3__{am,se}_scaffold.csv.gz reproduce the doc's geometry columns EXACTLY (S_AM 125,965 um2 computed vs 125,965 printed; d_h = (V_SE/0.72)/S_AM = 916.1 nm vs 916 printed; V_SE 83,089 um3 vs 83,089 at doc line 66) — so this bucket is the verified source bed and the only unreproducible number in those tables is the sigma cell. Contradicting sources, all in-repo: (a) same doc line 464 '| **ps_7_3** | **0.375** (0.1048 run) | **0.467** | * mismatch — source unknown |' and line 466 'the recorded 0.467 cannot be reproduced from any existing file'; (b) same doc line 554 '**ps_7_3 @ phi0.72 = 0.4226** (not the source-unknown 0.467 — that value's provenance problem is closed here)'; (c) CLAUDE.md: '192 quotation value = 5 beds -0.563 / R2 0.910 (all 5 points interpolated, 0 extrapolated). The old 4-bed -0.542/0.933 is history.' Yet doc line 130 still reads '| 0.72 | **0.7001** | 0.5457 | 0.4921 | 0.4671 | **0.3743** | **1.87x** |', line 153 '| ps_7_3 | 125,965 | 916 | 0.4671 |', line 156 '**log sigma vs log d_h : slope -0.541 . R2 0.935**' — with no correction marker anywhere in lines 126-160. Provenance for the correct value is present: docs/data/se_curve_metrics/xfer_kit_ps_7_3_g192_e{742,1173,1497}.json, platen_mach_V_over_cP = 0.03.
findings.proposed_action: Add an inline correction to the two tables (lines 130, 153): replace 0.4671 with 0.4226 or strike it with a pointer to the doc's own line 554, and re-label the line-156 slope as the superseded 4-bed/source-unknown fit, citing CLAUDE.md's -0.563 / R2 0.910 as current. The 1.87x headline itself is unaffected (both extremes are 0:10 and 10:0, both mach 0.03) — say so explicitly so the fix does not read as retracting the composition result. This is exactly the CLAUDE.md discipline-4 failure mode ('a commit that retracts a number fixes the ledger and derived docs in the same commit'): the correction landed in one section and never propagated to the tables above it.

findings.claim: All ten preserved runner scripts were edited in place AFTER preservation, so they are not the runners that produced the archived metrics; and the runner's default loading rate (V/c_P ~ 0.105) reproduces the discarded 0.1048-mach arm, not the mach-0.03 arm that CLAUDE.md says is the citable one. The preservation fidelity statement covers only the am/se scaffolds and never says this.
findings.evidence: git log --follow docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/kit_ps_7_3__run_mpm.sh returns two commits: 466926c53 (added) and 4c751ed65 (modified). git show --stat 4c751ed65 shows +18 lines to each of the five run_mpm.sh and +1 line to each run_a1_anchors.sh, inserted by scripts/patch_kit_quasistatic.py (its docstring: 'retroactively wires quasistatic-gate approval into ALREADY DISTRIBUTED kits'). The resulting default in every preserved run_mpm.sh is QS=(--allow-fast-platen), i.e. the geometric rule vmax=0.008*(WALL0-FLOOR), which the same file's own comment states gives 'V/c_P ~= 0.105' for these ~114 um beds. Contradicting sources: (a) scripts/unpack_kit_scaffolds.py:39-42 describes these files as what 'the ORIGINAL kit had in addition'; (b) docs/se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md:526-527 presents the preserved set under a 'gzip integrity 10/10' fidelity claim, and commit 466926c53's message scopes the byte-equality check to am/se only ('am/se preserved copies match the original tar 10/10 bytes'); (c) CLAUDE.md states the citable 192 5-bed fit uses mach 0.03 and that ps_7_3's 0.1048 runs were the source of the discarded 0.467 — and the mach-0.03 runs were driven by scripts/run_se_curve_batch.sh (see scripts/setup_v100.sh:192), which is NOT part of this preserved kit.
findings.proposed_action: Add one line to the run_mpm.sh header (or to docs/se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md section 8) stating: the runners were retro-patched on 2026-08-11 and are behaviour-preserving but not byte-original; re-running them reproduces the mach-0.1048 arm, and the citable mach-0.03 curve points come from scripts/run_se_curve_batch.sh --phi ... --n-grid 192, not from run_mpm.sh. Scope the existing '10/10 bytes' fidelity sentence explicitly to the am/se scaffolds, which is what was actually verified.

findings.claim: Five live, executable scripts regenerate STEP3 sigma in the retracted vox 0.4 / n_vox 192 convention with no retraction banner, and they sit outside the ban sweep's globs — the same generator-versus-output gap the repo already closed for build.js and the seminar deck generators.
findings.evidence: Every preserved run_mpm.sh runs 'python3 mpm_webapp_payload.py ... --n-vox 192 --step3-vox 0.4 --step3-gpu' and its trailing echo tells the user to 'upload mpm_payload.json + mpm_metrics.json back to the case in the webapp (step3.sigma_e_eff_S_cm = STEP3 sigma_e)'. Contradicting sources: docs/reviews/claims.json quotation_ban entries for CL-24 give the reason 'vox 0.4 point-stamp artifact; tightening the same convention walks it +42.15 -> +8.49 %' and CL-41 bans the vox 0.15/0.125/0.115 ratios as p1 plate-rule products; CLAUDE.md's SR-01 section states the 0.4 um headline 'is a product of the grid' and that vox 0.4 point-stamp 'is not a physical grid but an intensity probe (its sigma_e and gain absolute values stay in the banned series)'. Sweep coverage: scripts/check_review_findings.py:104-132 BAN_SCAN_GLOBS covers 'scripts/*.sh' but not 'docs/**/*.sh', so these ten .sh files are unread by the sweep; I ran all 22 quotation_ban patterns over the decompressed bucket by hand and got 0 hits today — the exposure is prospective, from re-running the generator, which is precisely the argument recorded at check_review_findings.py:113-124 for admitting docs/**/*.js.
findings.proposed_action: Add a two-line banner to the STEP2/payload section of the five run_mpm.sh pointing at claims.json CL-24/CL-41 and stating that vox 0.4 STEP3 sigma is a probe convention whose absolute sigma_e/sigma_ion gains are not quotable. Separately, extend BAN_SCAN_GLOBS with 'docs/**/*.sh' so preserved runners are swept like the deck and manuscript generators already are.

findings.claim: Eight of the fifteen preserved shell scripts are byte-identical redundant copies, and the in-code justification for keeping five copies of each asserts the opposite of what the bytes say.
findings.evidence: md5sum over the directory: all five *__harvest.sh = 2fa7e74b200f07c3da27547e6a8e40e1; all five *__run_a1_anchors.sh = 79aade13bfeea8e41679ea43ded5d87a; only *__run_mpm.sh yields five distinct hashes, and diffing two of them shows exactly 3 substantive lines (case id, --fibre-align, --target-porosity). They are identical because both scripts address every input as "$KIT/am_scaffold.csv" etc., so they are kit-independent by construction. Contradicting source: scripts/unpack_kit_scaffolds.py:39-42 comment — 'the original kit also had a fracture_scaffold and THREE RUNNERS THAT DIFFER PER KIT (all 5 kit hashes differ = you must not keep just one copy)' — and commit 466926c53's message repeats it verbatim ('per-kit differing runners, 3 kinds (all hashes differ)'). Both are false for two of the three runner kinds.
findings.proposed_action: Correct the comment at unpack_kit_scaffolds.py:39-42 to say only run_mpm.sh is kit-specific. For v3, either keep a single shared harvest.sh / run_a1_anchors.sh at the directory root and have unpack fan it out to each kit dir, or keep the copies but drop the false rationale. Low stakes (about 44 KB) — the point is that the stated reason for the redundancy is measurably wrong, so a future cleanup would be blocked by a bad argument.

findings.claim: The recorded preservation scope no longer matches the directory: it names 3 members per kit where there are now 7, and the commit that created the archive claims kit_real14 was preserved alongside the five kit_ps beds when it was not — real14 lives elsewhere, in a different format, and the unpack tool cannot restore it.
findings.evidence: docs/se_curve_transfer_verdict_20260806.md:526 states 'preservation scope: 5 kits x {am,se}_scaffold.csv.gz + mpm_input.json'. The directory holds 7 members per kit (fracture_scaffold.csv.gz + run_mpm.sh + harvest.sh + run_a1_anchors.sh were added 2026-08-11 by commit 466926c53), and scripts/unpack_kit_scaffolds.py:37-45 already lists all seven in MEMBERS. Separately, commit 986fa7bcb's message says 'kit_ps_{0_10,3_7,5_5,7_3,10_0} + kit_real14 am/se scaffolds (gzip)' but no kit_real14 file exists in docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/ (ls: 35 files, all kit_ps_*); real14 is preserved as docs/data/real14_am_scaffold.csv and docs/data/real14_se_scaffold.csv — plain, uncompressed, no mpm_input.json, and outside the '<kit>__<member>' naming that unpack_kit_scaffolds.discover() scans for, so 'kit_real14' can never be unpacked. real14 is the sixth bed of the same experiment (docs/data/se_curve_metrics/xfer_kit_real14_g192_*.json, 5 runs) and is the REAL14_SE_CURVE source CLAUDE.md relies on.
findings.proposed_action: Update the scope sentence to the actual 7 members. Either move real14_{am,se}_scaffold.csv into this directory under the kit_real14__ convention (adding a kit_real14__mpm_input.json with lateral_box so the fit tools can read it), or add one line to the doc and to unpack_kit_scaffolds.py's docstring saying real14 is deliberately stored separately and how to assemble it — right now a reader following the commit message looks for a file that is not there.

findings.claim: Four of the five manifests still declare am_material_class_mode = 'sdcp_mono_amp', a convention the generator records as abolished on 2026-08-04 because it mislabelled particles and poisoned corpus columns. I checked the data: no kit is actually affected, and nothing outside the generator reads the field — so this is a stale flag, not a defect, and that should be written down rather than re-derived by the next reader.
findings.evidence: Manifests: kit_ps_{3_7,5_5,7_3,10_0} carry 'am_material_class_mode': 'sdcp_mono_amp'; kit_ps_0_10 alone carries the post-fix 'mono_absolute_3.5um'. Contradicting source: scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py:565 comment 'material size-classification path (2026-08-04: the sdcp_mono_amp convention is ABOLISHED — every path is now size-based)', and lines 424-431 describe the incident it caused ('the 0:10 case, 4587 particles all r=2um = small, was recorded as type1 (AM_P) -> mpm_metrics reported coverage_AM_P=76.6 / AM_S=0.0 -> (a) the corpus coverage_AM_P and mpm_plastic_gain_AM_P columns mix 6um and 2um values, (b) physically-SC 2um particles get POLY expansion = wrong sign'). Measurement that closes it: the (type, radius) mapping in every am_scaffold is size-consistent — 0_10 {(2, 2.0um): 4587}, 3_7 {(1, 6.0): 55, (2, 2.0): 3207}, 5_5 {(1, 6.0): 88, (2, 2.0): 2292}, 7_3 {(1, 6.0): 126, (2, 2.0): 1372}, 10_0 {(1, 6.0): 175} — so the legacy label produced correct output here (the mono bed it would have broken, 0_10, is the one that carries the new label). A repo-wide grep for am_material_class_mode returns exactly one hit outside docs/data: mpm_input_from_case.py:566, the writer.
findings.proposed_action: Record the verification rather than re-run it: add a note to the kit index / v3 hub that the four sdcp_mono_amp manifests are a stale build-time label from 2026-04-21 and were checked size-consistent on 2026-09-09, and that the field has no consumer. Do not regenerate the manifests — the label is a truthful record of what the generator did, and rewriting it would break the tie to the 260421_* cases.

surface_worthy.why: This is the repo's cleanest controlled comparison and its geometry half is fully reproducible with no GPU, yet it is only reachable by reading to line 116 of a 560-line verdict doc. Five beds that differ in P:S alone: SE/solid 34.18-35.10 % (I recomputed all five from the scaffolds and they match the doc's column to the printed digit), thickness within +/-1.8 %, identical 50x50 um lateral box, n_SE within 0.05 %. The whole d_h collapse — S_AM and d_h for all five — falls out of these files in seconds: S_AM 230,568 / 186,083 / 155,019 / 125,965 / 79,168 um2 and d_h 500.7 / 620.3 / 744.5 / 916.1 / 1458.1 nm, each matching the canon table exactly. A v3 hub reader who wants to know what a 'controlled electrode comparison' looks like in this repo should land here, not on the retracted sigma column above it.
surface_worthy.one_line: Five P:S-only electrode beds whose SE/solid, S_AM and channel width d_h all recompute exactly from the preserved scaffolds — the d_h collapse is verifiable without a GPU.

surface_worthy.why: These five files hold a per-particle Auerbach fracture classification (worst_stage_rank 0..4 plus f_over_pc) for every AM particle in all five compositions, and nothing in docs/ or wiki/ tabulates it — only the FILE FORMAT is documented (docs/fracture_to_mpm_crackvoid.md:19). The measurement is striking and directly answers an open CLAUDE.md question. Distribution I computed: kit_ps_10_0 (mono 6um) 65.7 % at rank 3 and 2.3 % pulverised, median f/P_c = 14.1; kit_ps_0_10 (mono 2um) 75.1 % at rank 2, median f/P_c = 4.6; the three bimodal beds 76.8-86.9 % INTACT with median f/P_c = 0.24-0.37, i.e. 40-60x lower contact load per particle. So bimodal packing shields AM from fracture and both mono endpoints are bad in opposite ways. CLAUDE.md's 'grain size = closed design window' section explicitly names 'whether our Auerbach fracture responds there' as a literature-anchor validation target — the AM-side answer is already sitting in these files, unread.
surface_worthy.one_line: Per-particle fracture stage for all five P:S beds, never tabulated: bimodal beds are 77-87 % intact while both mono endpoints are heavily fractured (median f/P_c 0.24-0.37 vs 4.6-14.1).

surface_worthy.why: The temperature_provenance and a1_pressure_provenance blocks in these manifests are canon-grade prose buried in a data file. They state which physics is and is not temperature-dependent (sigma_ion via Kraft-2017 Arrhenius and i0 via the kim2025 R_ct anchor are wired as a PAIR — 'giving only one flips the overpotential sign or produces a false label'; D_s, OCP dU/dT, sigma_e, kappa and SE hardness are 25 C constants for want of an anchor), and they carry an explicit prohibition: 'Ea is a BAND 0.29-0.46 eV (1.8x wide = x2.47..x4.44 from 30->60 C); single-value reporting is forbidden — sweep EA_ION_EV_BAND.' Likewise a1_pressure_provenance records rate_dependence = NOT_MODELLED_rate_independent_J2 and how to verify an unload actually reached operating pressure. This is the kind of scope statement a reader needs before quoting any temperature-swept number, and it exists only inside 5 JSON payloads that no doc quotes.
surface_worthy.one_line: Kit manifests carry an explicit temperature- and pressure-scope contract, including a standing ban on single-value Ea reporting, that no document reproduces.

verdict: This is a coherent, complete, single-campaign raw-data family, not a dead one-off: the 18 files are the entire measurement output of the D13 pellet ion calibration (prereg docs/reviews/sdcp_ion_calib_prereg_20260825.md, tool scripts/pellet_rve_sigma.py, runner scripts/run_pellet_calib.sh), a synthetic non-overlapping RSA pellet RVE - uniform LPSCl matrix filling a 6 um box at vox 0.12, 9:1 wt binder spheres of D 0.30 um, x/y periodic, z plates, 4 seeds per arm. It contains one identity check (neat), a six-point PTFE blocking sweep b in {0, 0.12, 0.17, 0.21, 0.24, 0.36} um, a four-point SDCP ion-conductivity bracket {2, 5, 6.2, 10}e-4 S/cm, two sensitivity axes (rho_SDCP 1.1/1.7, binder D 0.6/1.2), and two STAGE 2 electronic arms (T1 frozen-knob prediction, and the SDCP electronic ceiling probe). All four seeds per file have distinct input_digest values (the digest hashes the actual phase grid), no arm reports non-convergence, and I found zero hits against all 22 patterns in the claims.json quotation_ban registry - these are pellet ion numbers on a different axis from the retracted CL-24/CL-33/CL-41 sigma_e gain families, so nothing here is a silent leak. It is still the canonical copy and it must not be archived away or regenerated: findings.json R18-1 cites ptfe_ion_blk0.12.json by path, claims.json CL-62 quotes the xstar confirmation run in its bridge field, CL-59 uses this batch's x* as its RSA scenario (r = 0.1737), scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py quotes it in the --sigma-ion-sdcp help text, and docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md §5 proposes the blk* sweep as an input to an open CL-81 measurement. The known defect of the batch - a mixed matrix conductivity, 3.0e-3 on eight arms and 3.57e-3 on the other ten - is already caught and correctly recorded in d13_prereg_v2_20260830.md §8-1b and fixed forward in the runner, and the docs normalise correctly by each arm's own sigma_SE, so I am not re-reporting it; the shared bed digests across sdcp_ion / sdcp_e_ceiling / the four x-sweep files are likewise deliberate (they are the F_e == F_ion control), not duplicates. What a v3 reorganisation should do: (1) treat this directory as an immutable dated archive and stop the runner defaulting its output into it, since a bare re-run would overwrite 12 of the 18 files at the new convention; (2) add the manifest the directory lacks (per-file command, sigma_SE, code_sha, prereg id) so reproduction stops requiring a three-document join; (3) close the two stale statements that still say the raw data is absent - it is present and I verified every transcribed digit against it; and (4) surface the formation-factor table and the UNREACHABLE bracket, because those, not the raw sigma values, are the only forms of this batch that can be cited.
