findings.claim: The committed runner's default output directory is this archive, and it now runs a different convention than the archive holds. Re-running scripts/run_pellet_calib.sh with no arguments silently overwrites 12 of these 18 files - 8 of them at a different matrix conductivity - destroying the only raw evidence behind a live ledger finding.
findings.evidence: scripts/run_pellet_calib.sh:25 'OUT=${OUT:-docs/data/pellet_calib_20260825}' and :35 'SIG0=${SIG0:-3.57e-3}'. The runner emits exactly neat_ion, sdcp_ion, ptfe_ion_blk{0,0.12,0.17,0.21,0.24,0.36}, sdcp_ion_rho{1.1,1.7}, ptfe_ion_d{0.6,1.2} = 12 of the 18 committed names. Eight of those are archived at sigma_ion_se 3.0e-3 (neat_ion, sdcp_ion, blk0, blk0.12, blk0.24, blk0.36, rho1.1, rho1.7, d0.6, d1.2 - verified from each file's arm.sigma_ion_se), so a default re-run overwrites them with 3.57e-3 values under the same filenames, in a directory named for 2026-08-25, at a newer code_sha than the 'bb361b64 / f286ac74' generation the freeze doc pins. docs/reviews/findings.json R18-1 cites docs/data/pellet_calib_20260825/ptfe_ion_blk0.12.json by path as its evidence.
findings.proposed_action: Point the runner default at a dated output directory (e.g. docs/data/pellet_calib_<today>) and make it refuse to write into an existing non-empty directory; or mark this directory read-only in the v3 layout with a one-line PROVENANCE note (2026-08-25 batch, mixed sigma_SE, superseded convention). Do not silently reuse the name.

findings.claim: docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md proposes using this PTFE ion-blocking sweep to bound the additive mismatch in the CONTACT_FREE gap measurement, and names as a prerequisite 'first confirm whether that sweep is a real bed or a synthetic pellet'. The answer is in the files: it is a synthetic RSA pellet with no active material at ~9 vol% PTFE, i.e. roughly ten times the binder loading of the electrode arms it would be bounding.
findings.evidence: Data: every ptfe_ion_blk*.json row carries wt_binder 0.1, vol_target 0.09174311926605504, vol_stamped 0.091792, n_spheres 1422, box_um 6.0, and no AM phase; scripts/pellet_rve_sigma.py docstring states the RVE is the '9:1 wt LPSCl:binder' pellet built by non-overlapping RSA with an SE matrix filling the box (no active material at all). Contradicting source: docs/voxel_contact_free_gap.md:205-206 proposes '(b) 첨가제 불일치를 리포의 PTFE 이온-차단 스윕(docs/data/pellet_calib_20260825/ptfe_ion_blk*.json)으로 경계 지어 보정 - 선행 확인: 그 스윕이 실침대인지 합성 펠릿인지', while the electrode arms it must bound are PTFE 1.0 wt% (SBE) / 0.5 wt% (DBE) per CLAUDE.md and claims.json CL-59.
findings.proposed_action: Record the prerequisite answer in voxel_contact_free_gap.md §5: synthetic non-overlapping RSA pellet, 9:1 wt binder:SE = 9.17 vol% PTFE, no AM, box 6 um / vox 0.12 / 4 seeds. Then state whether option (b) survives that composition gap - a ~9 vol% binder-only pellet cannot bound a ~1 wt% electrode without an explicit rescaling argument, so either the rescaling is written down or option (b) is dropped in favour of option (a).

findings.claim: The prereg and the runner both state, as the load-bearing diagnosis for why two readers mis-compared this batch, that the JSON does not record the formation factor. It does - every row carries formation_factor_ion. Only the agg summary block omits it, and the per-row field is strictly more informative than the batch-mean [F] table the runner was given as the remedy.
findings.evidence: Data: docs/data/pellet_calib_20260825/neat_ion.json line 41 '"formation_factor_ion": 1.0000000000004152'; present on all 4 rows of all 18 files (e.g. ptfe_ion_blk0.17 rows give F = [0.201101, 0.192561, 0.204712, 0.204942], per-seed, which the runner's batch-mean table cannot give). Written by scripts/pellet_rve_sigma.py:176-177. Contradicting sources: docs/reviews/d13_prereg_v2_20260830.md §8-1 '진짜 위험은 JSON 이 F 를 안 적는다는 것이다 (sigma_ion_eff_mS_cm_mean 만 있다)' and scripts/run_pellet_calib.sh:28-29 '그런데 JSON 은 F 를 안 적고 sigma_ion_eff_mS_cm_mean 만 적는다'.

Keep the [F] table and the single-sigma_SE fix - the remedy is right, only the diagnosis is wrong. Optionally add formation_factor_ion_mean to agg so the summary block is self-sufficient.

findings.claim: The directory has no manifest or README, and six of the eighteen files are not produced by the committed runner. Four of those six have no committed command line anywhere in the repo - their parameters survive only inside each file's own arm block.
findings.evidence: ls of docs/data/pellet_calib_20260825/ returns 18 .json files and nothing else. scripts/run_pellet_calib.sh emits exactly 12 of the 18 names. docs/reviews/pellet_calib_freeze_20260825.md §4b gives explicit command lines for exactly two more (sdcp_ion_xstar.json, ptfe_e_frozen.json). The remaining four - sdcp_e_ceiling.json, sdcp_ion_x0.0002.json, sdcp_ion_x0.0005.json, sdcp_ion_x0.0010.json - appear in no script and in no committed command; their numbers appear only as prose in freeze §3 ('x=0 -> 2.537 / 0.2e-3 -> 2.661 / 0.5e-3 -> 2.813 / 1.0e-3 -> 3.010'). None of the 18 files records a code_sha, argv, timestamp or prereg id; the code generation (bb361b64 for STAGE 1, f286ac74 for STAGE 2) is recorded only in the freeze doc.
findings.proposed_action: Add a one-page manifest to the directory: batch date, prereg id (sdcp_ion_calib_prereg_20260825.md), code_sha per stage, the exact command for each of the 18 files, and the sigma_SE actually used per file. Reproduction is possible today (each arm block is a complete parameter dump) but it takes a three-document join.

surface_worthy.why: This is the repo's cleanest standing accuracy witness for the STEP3 finite-volume solver that produces every voxel sigma number in the project: a uniform block returns the input conductivity to 4e-13 relative. It is currently visible only as a passing remark in one section of one review doc, and voxel_contact_free_gap.md already had to reach for it.
surface_worthy.one_line: Uniform-matrix identity check: sigma_eff = 3.000000000001246 mS/cm from sigma_in = 3.0 mS/cm, formation factor 1.0000000000004152 (4 seeds).

surface_worthy.why: The formation factor F = sigma_eff/sigma_SE is the only convention-invariant, citable form of this whole bucket - it is what survives the mixed matrix conductivity in the 2026-08-25 batch - and it exists only as a hand-built table inside d13_prereg_v2_20260830.md §8-1, not next to the data or in any hub.

The PTFE calibration's actual outcome is a negative result - the experimental target is unreachable because the blocking knob is quantised to EDT voxel shells - and readers keep re-deriving or mis-reading it as a successful calibration. It needs to sit with the data, not only in a post-hoc banner.
surface_worthy.one_line: Normalised to a single sigma_SE the target 0.97 mS/cm falls strictly between two adjacent shells (b=0.12 -> 1.5175, b=0.17 -> 0.7170); no b reaches it, so the answer is a bracket, and the frozen b=0.17 sits -26.1 % below target.

surface_worthy.why: This single file is the raw evidence behind a number quoted in production code help text and used as one of three scenarios in a live ledger claim, yet nothing outside two review docs points at it. A v3 hub reader asking 'where does sigma_ion(SDCP)* = 0.62e-3 come from' currently has no path to the measurement.
surface_worthy.one_line: Confirmation run at x* = 6.2e-4 S/cm gives 2.8654779602491254 mS/cm against the 2.86 target (+0.19 %, seed SE(log10) 9.2e-05, 4/4 seeds) - convention-bound to this pellet RVE, transplant into electrode runs forbidden.

surface_worthy.why: The bucket quantifies how far this RVE convention departs from the Bruggeman dilution it is nominally near, which is the number that decides whether any phase sigma calibrated here can travel. It is stated once in the freeze doc and nowhere else.
surface_worthy.one_line: Negative control against Bruggeman dilution: PTFE stamp-only -6.0 %, SDCP -9.95 % (the RVE over-dilutes, and the fitted phase sigma back-fills that excess - which is why the calibrated value is convention-bound).

verdict: This bucket is five MPM run kits for the Phase A 6 mAh composition-ordering campaign (case input_6mAh_real_4, P:S 7:3), generated 2026-09-07 by scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py and committed so the GPU run would need no file transfer. Each kit is three files: a per-arm run_mpm.sh (the only file that differs between arms), a base-bed mpm_input.json (byte-identical across all five), and a generic harvest.sh (byte-identical across all five and to five more copies under docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/). They are inputs, not measurements — no kit file contains a measured value, so carries_banned_value is false for all fifteen. This is emphatically NOT a dead one-off sweep: scripts/phase_a_plan.py:245 names these files the canon runner, four of the five arms completed on the kgy 3090 on 2026-09-08 (CL-85), and the newest ledger entry CL-88 (2026-09-09) declares the follow-on 96-arm STEP3 campaign cleared to proceed. They must survive the v3 reorganization intact and stay adjacent to the two .gz scaffolds they read. Two problems make them not currently canonical. First, all five run_mpm.sh are one generation stale: commit 3279cfa90 (2026-09-08, 'Rule N: the kit runner logged a loading rate it was not using') fixed the generator so the runner prints its real QS array, but the kits were last baked 2026-09-07 and still echo '기하 규칙 유지' while passing --platen-mach 0.03 — and Rule N cannot see them, because check_kit_rate_label opens only the generator's own path, so CI is green on exactly the artifacts the rule exists to protect. That is the CLAUDE.md ⑤ false-green pattern one rule after it was written down. Second, the ledger has drifted away from the kits rather than the reverse: CL-78 is still status live carrying SE 158,651 / porosity 14.283 % / d_h 0.9810, all three retired by commit 0d5ede878, which fixed the README and the kits and never touched claims.json — the shipped se_scaffold.csv.gz has exactly 158,688 rows, so the kits are right and the canon is wrong. The v3 action list is short and mechanical: regenerate the five kits, widen Rule N to glob committed runners, correct CL-78 and the prereg §9-2 count table, give the Lee arm (VGCF_PTFE_3_0.5) a row in README §② and precompute.json so the folder's canon covers all five kits it ships, and put a ⛔ line on the kits' closing instruction that currently routes the vox-0.4 σ_e into the webapp with no marker.

findings.claim: All five committed run_mpm.sh print a loading-rate label they are not using. Line 77 sets QS=(--platen-mach 0.03 --allow-fast-platen); line 83 then echoes '준정적: 기하 규칙 유지' (quasi-static: geometric rule retained) into mpm_run.log. This is the exact defect that commit 3279cfa90 (2026-09-08) 'Rule N: the kit runner logged a loading rate it was not using' was created to eliminate — the fix landed in the generator only, one day after these kits were last baked (0d5ede878, 2026-09-07), so all five shipped copies still carry it.
findings.evidence: Data file: grep -n '기하 규칙 유지' docs/data/phase_a_6mah/kits/*/run_mpm.sh returns 5 hits, all on line 83, all on echo lines (not comments). Same files line 77: QS=(--platen-mach 0.03 --allow-fast-platen). Contradicting sources: (a) scripts/check_method_discipline.py:2036 _KIT_RATE_BANNED = ('기하 규칙 유지',) with the docstring '**Mach 0.03 으로 도는 Phase A W4 런의 로그가 기하 규칙이라고 거짓 보고**했다 ... 런을 보는 사람이 로그만 읽고 규약을 오판하거나 멀쩡한 런을 폐기할 수 있다'; (b) README.md:109 '⛔ 기하 규칙으로 되돌리는 개정은 허용되지 않는다 (Codex R9)'; (c) README.md:131 'W1·W2 실측은 exploratory pilot 이다 — 본 판정에서 제외한다. 기하 규칙(Mach 0.4275/0.4393)으로 돌았고 등록 규약(0.03)이 아니다'; (d) scripts/phase_a_plan.py:245 names these very files 정본. harvest.sh:19 bundles mpm_run.log as audit provenance, so the false label travels into every harvested tarball. Phase A is live: CL-88 (2026-09-09) says '96 팔 진행 조건이 충족'.
findings.proposed_action: Regenerate all five kits from the current scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py (which now echoes ${QS[*]}) and commit; nothing else about the kits changes. Until then, any Phase-A run log reading '기하 규칙 유지' must be checked against mpm_metrics.json platen_mach_VcP before being labelled a pilot or quoted in Methods.

findings.claim: Rule N is a false-green on exactly the artifacts it exists to protect: check_kit_rate_label() reads one hardcoded path, _KIT_GEN = 'scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py', and never looks at the generated kits on disk. CI prints '✓ 킷 러너가 재하율을 QS 실물로 보고한다 (하드코딩 라벨 없음)' while five committed kit runners each carry the banned string on an echo line.
findings.evidence: scripts/check_method_discipline.py:2035 _KIT_GEN = 'scripts/mpm_input_from_case.py'; :2048 s = src if src is not None else open(os.path.join(ROOT, _KIT_GEN)) — the only file ever opened. Ran `python3 scripts/check_method_discipline.py`: output '규칙 N — 킷 러너의 재하율 라벨이 실물인가 / ✓ 킷 러너가 재하율을 QS 실물로 보고한다 (하드코딩 라벨 없음)' and overall '✓ 방법론 규율: 0 오류'. Simultaneously grep -n '기하 규칙 유지' docs/data/phase_a_6mah/kits/*/run_mpm.sh = 5 hits on echo lines. Contradicting source: CLAUDE.md rule ⑤ '부분집합 필터로 훑으면 조용히 초록이 된다 … 필터를 버리고 실물을 잡는다 … 후보를 고르는 코드가 곧 사각지대다' — same failure class, one rule later.
findings.proposed_action: Extend check_kit_rate_label to glob every committed runner (docs/data/**/kits/*/run_mpm.sh and docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/*__run_mpm.sh) in addition to the generator, with the same echo-lines-only narrowing and the same N-5 comments-pass selftest. It fails today on 5 files, which is the point.

findings.claim: Ledger CL-78 (status live) still carries the retired bed constants that commit 0d5ede878 replaced in the kits and the README. Under the canon rule 'the ledger outranks prose', a reader takes CL-78's SE 158,651 / porosity 14.283 % / d_h 0.9810 over the shipped kit's 158,688 / 14.321 % / 0.9821 — and the shipped scaffold itself proves the kit right.
findings.evidence: Kit file: mpm_input.json has "n_SE": 158688 and "target_porosity": 0.1432 (identical in all five kits). Independent check of the shipped scaffold: gunzip docs/data/phase_a_6mah/se_scaffold.csv.gz → exactly 158,688 data rows, all type 3. README.md:42-45 declares 'SE 158,688' and 'porosity 14.321 % ← **정본**' and :53 '초판에서 내가 따로 필터한 158,651 판은 폐기했다'. docs/data/phase_a_6mah/precompute.json totals: porosity 0.14320961, n_se 158688, d_h_um 0.98214897, phi_se_local 0.67160578. Contradicting source: claims.json CL-78 measured.value literally reads 'SE 158,651 (R 0.5)' and 'porosity **14.283 %** (옛 기록 14.28 와 일치)' and '① d_h = **0.9810 µm** · φ_SE_local 0.6723'. Commit 0d5ede878's own message says 'Porosity had two canons, 14.321 in the README and 14.283 in the kits ... Unified on 14.321', and git show --name-only 0d5ede878 shows claims.json was NOT touched; claims.json has since been committed three more times (through 2026-09-09) with CL-78 unchanged. Secondary mismatch in the same block: CL-78 ② and prereg §9-2 give VGCF 1 → 26,967 and VGCF 4 → 111,275, while the sealed precompute.json additive_counts (code_sha 8aa69af3, code_dirty false) and README §② give 26,968 and 111,279.
findings.proposed_action: Correct CL-78's measured.value in place (SE 158,688 · porosity 14.321 % · d_h 0.9821 · φ 0.6716 · counts 26,968/111,279) with a note that the 158,651/14.283 variant is the retired pre-unification filter, and fix the prereg §9-2 count table to match the sealed precompute. This is CLAUDE.md rule ④ ('수치를 철회하는 커밋은 같은 커밋에서 원장·파생 문서를 고친다') applied one commit late.

findings.claim: The kits compute STEP3 at --step3-vox 0.4 and their closing instructions tell the operator to upload the result to the webapp and paint it as *the* STEP3 σ_e, with no ⛔ marker — while the campaign's own prereg and ledger forbid citing any vox-0.4 σ_e from these runs. The quotation_ban registry has no pattern for these values, and the ban sweep cannot read JSON, so once the number reaches mpm_metrics.json and the viewer nothing checks it.
findings.evidence: Kit file line 104: --step3-vox 0.4; line 112: 'upload mpm_payload.json + mpm_metrics.json back to the case in the webapp'; line 113: '(additive run이면 mpm_metrics.json의 step3.sigma_e_eff_S_cm = STEP3 σ_e — viewer 전류밀도 모드로 색칠)'. Contradicting sources: prereg phase_a_6mah_order_prereg_20260907.md:414 '⚠ 이 런의 STEP3 는 킷 기본 vox 0.4 다 — **σ 값은 판정 대상이 아니다**' and :271 '⛔ vox 0.4 = 인용 금지'; CL-84 '⛔ **이 값은 판정 대상이 아니다**'; CL-85 '⛔ ③ 의 값은 등록 격자가 아니라 판정 대상이 아니다'. Magnitude of the exposure is measured: CL-88 reports the same bed pair at 772× (vox 0.4) versus 55.6× (vox 0.25) — 14× apart. README.md:140 adds that SE necks are already 85.6 % / 97.4 % unresolved at h = 0.20 / 0.25 (CL-72), i.e. worse at 0.4. claims.json quotation_ban (22 patterns) contains no Phase-A entry.
findings.proposed_action: Add one ⛔ line to the kit's closing echo ('step3.sigma_e_eff_S_cm here is vox 0.4 = wiring/direction only, not a judgment value — Phase A σ_e comes from the separate 96-arm run at 0.25/0.20/0.15'), and register the Phase-A vox-0.4 ratios in quotation_ban so the sweep covers them if they ever reach Markdown or a deck.

findings.claim: The file harvest.sh bundles as the run's provenance record is byte-identical across all five kits and records none of the axis the campaign varies. It carries no add_recipe, no dilate_z, no fibre_align, and a target_porosity (0.1432) that is not the value the payload step actually targets for any arm.
findings.evidence: md5sum */mpm_input.json = 7e6a4302a7919dfa17cdf083cf49c728 for all five. The composition axis lives only in run_mpm.sh argv: --add-recipe VGCF:PTFE={1:1, 2:1, 3:0.5, 3:1, 4:1}, --dilate-z {1.0214, 1.0519, 1.0795, 1.0798, 1.1085}, payload --target-porosity {0.1447, 0.1532, 0.1589, 0.1589, 0.1645} — none of which appears in mpm_input.json, whose target_porosity is the undilated 0.1432. harvest.sh:18-21 bundles exactly 'mpm_payload.json mpm_metrics.json mpm_input.json mpm_run.log' under the comment '── geometry / provenance (STEP2 산출 — 뷰어와 감사에 필수, 작음) ──'. So a harvested tarball's declared provenance file cannot tell an auditor which arm it came from; recovery depends on mpm_run.log's RUN_DIR name — the same log that mis-states the loading rate (finding 1). Note also the rounding collision: kits 3_0.5 and 3_1 both pass --target-porosity 0.1589 despite different dilate_z.
findings.proposed_action: Have mpm_input_from_case.py write add_recipe, dilate_z, fibre_align, platen_mach, frames and the payload target_porosity into mpm_input.json (the schema is already extended conditionally at :569), so the one file harvest.sh calls provenance actually identifies the arm.

findings.claim: The Lee-2025 comparison arm ships as a fifth kit but is documented only in a script. The data folder's own canon covers four arms: README §② lists four recipes, precompute.json additive_counts has four entries, CL-78 ② has four rows, CL-85 reports four completed beds. Nothing in docs/ or the ledger maps VGCF_PTFE_3_0.5 to the prereg's Secondary arm, and it has no sealed additive object count to check its --dilate-z 1.0795 against.
findings.evidence: Identity is recoverable only from scripts/phase_a_plan.py:68 'LEE_RECIPE = \'VGCF=3,PTFE=0.5\'  # Lee 2025 첨가제 wt%' and :39 'STEP2 4 조성 (VGCF 1/2/3/4 + PTFE 1) + Lee 1 = 5 런'. Contradicting sources: README.md:62 file table says '킷 **5개**' but README.md:144-149 §② tabulates only VGCF{1,2,3,4}+PTFE1; docs/data/phase_a_6mah/precompute.json 'additive_counts' contains exactly four objects, none with ptfe_wt_pct 0.5; claims.json CL-78 ② lists four recipes; CL-85 'Phase A 네 침대(VGCF 1·2·3·4 wt%, PTFE 1) 가 ... 전부 완주했다'. grep -rn 'VGCF_PTFE_3_0\.5' across docs/, scripts/, wiki/, webapp/ returns nothing outside the kit directory and the audit residual list. Prereg §1 rule ① states '설계 격자점이 하나라도 비면 **판정하지 않는다**', so an undocumented fifth kit sitting beside the 4×3×8 matrix is a contamination risk in both directions.
findings.proposed_action: Add a Lee row (VGCF 3 + PTFE 0.5) to README §② and to precompute.json's additive_counts by re-running phase_a_precompute.py with that recipe, and state in the README file table that the fifth kit is the prereg's Secondary Lee-2025 absolute-comparison arm and is excluded from the 96-arm primary matrix.

findings.claim: harvest.sh exists in ten byte-identical copies in the repo — five here and five in docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/ — and is emitted verbatim by the generator. This is duplication by design (a kit must be a self-contained zip), so a v3 reorganization should record it as intentional rather than dedupe it.

verdict: This is a live, load-bearing, cheap-to-reproduce measurement family — not a dead one-off sweep, and it should survive a v3 reorganization intact. All 18 files are CPU rasterize-only phase ledgers (no solve) of one DBE bed and its SBE negative control (case 260714_145738_778fa4), counting cells per phase (sid 0 pore / 1 AM_S / 3 VGCF / 5 SDCP / 6 SE) across six voxel edges (0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.15, 0.125, 0.1) and two SDCP stamp conventions (point vs true-diameter sphere Ø0.30). They landed in two commits on 2026-08-18: 07c767a56 (10 files, CL-43 phase displacement) and b6092ace1 (8 files, prereg v3 STEP 1). They are still the canonical and only copy of these counts — phase_ledger_grid.json is a derived summary that quotes a strict subset, and there is no finer or corrected re-run of any grid, so nothing here is superseded. I verified every one of the 18: sum(cells_by_sid) == product(grid_shape) exactly, and the numbers reproduce the claims that cite them to the digit — sphere-stamp ratio 0.9858 / 0.9841 / 0.9839 (CLAUDE.md's 0.986/0.984/0.984), point-stamp 0.2378 / 0.1378 / 0.0706 (0.238/0.138/0.071), and conductive dof 26,931,599 / 45,362,494 / 86,768,963 (the 45.4 M and 86.8 M in CLAUDE.md). carries_banned_value is false for all 18: I swept every one of the 22 quotation_ban patterns across the files and got zero hits, which is expected — these rows hold integer cell counts, grid shapes and voxel edges, never a sigma value or a gain ratio, so the CSV/JSON blind spot in the ban sweep is not exercised here. Three things a v3 reorganization needs to know. (1) The bucket has one P1, and it is not in these files but in a document that failed to read them: the Methods/SI draft still prints the grid as 334 x 334 x 484 where all four vox-0.15 ledgers say 490 — already registered as CL-86 item (b), confirmed here from the raw side. (2) The derived summary phase_ledger_grid.json has two arithmetically wrong rows, both in the pair added later (vox 0.125's single_particle_arithmetic is 0.1414 instead of 0.1382, and vox 0.1's delta_pct is +0.4 where it should be -0.14, a sign that contradicts that file's own 'the arithmetic is an upper bound' reading); the ledgers themselves are correct, so the fix is a recompute from them. (3) The rows are log transcriptions and dropped every convention field the writer emits — no bridge_um, no sdcp_sphere_d_um, no origin_shift_um — so the report tool warns on all 18 that it is assuming Ø0.30, and the 'converged at 0.984' verdict rests on a diameter that is inferred from the filename convention rather than recorded. That is the one thing worth spending effort on: backfill four fields, or re-emit from the rasterizer, which costs minutes of CPU and no GPU. Finally, do not dedupe the three SBE _pt/_sph pairs that look byte-identical — the identity IS the negative control.

findings.claim: The two newest rows of sdcp_point_stamp_vs_grid (vox 0.125 and vox 0.1) carry derived columns that are wrong and that contradict the same file's own _reading. The vox-0.1 row reports delta_pct +0.4, i.e. measured representation volume ABOVE the single-particle arithmetic — but _reading states the arithmetic is a weak UPPER bound, so the delta must be <= 0. Recomputing straight from the ledger cell counts gives -0.14. The vox-0.125 row's single_particle_arithmetic 0.1414 is wrong (0.125^3 / 0.014137166941154067 = 0.13816), which propagates a delta_pct of -2.4 where the true value is -0.24, a factor of ten. The four original grids (0.4/0.3/0.25/0.15) all recompute correctly, so the error is confined to the two rows added in the later prereg v3 STEP 1 commit.
findings.evidence: Data files: ledger_DBE_v0125_pt.json sid 5 = 138,654 cells; ledger_DBE_v01_pt.json sid 5 = 138,794 cells. Recomputed against phase_ledger_grid.json _fixed (sdcp_true_volume_um3_each 0.014137166941154067, sdcp_particles 138988): vox 0.125 measured 0.13782 / arithmetic 0.13816 / delta -0.24 %; vox 0.1 measured 0.07064 / arithmetic 0.07074 / delta -0.14 %. File states: {vox 0.125, single_particle_arithmetic 0.1414, delta_pct -2.4} and {vox 0.1, single_particle_arithmetic 0.0707, delta_pct 0.4}. Contradicting source: the same file's _reading — 'the single-particle arithmetic is a WEAK UPPER BOUND on the real bed ... it comes out lower by -0.4 %(0.15) to -4.8 %(0.4)'. A positive delta is outside the stated bound. claims.json CL-25's own table lists only the four original grids with correct deltas, so the ledger is clean and only this derived file is wrong.
findings.proposed_action: Recompute both rows from the ledgers: vox 0.125 -> single_particle_arithmetic 0.1382, delta_pct -0.2; vox 0.1 -> delta_pct -0.1 (compute the delta from the full-precision ratio, not from the 3-decimal rounded measured value, which is what flipped the sign at 0.1). Extend _reading's stated range to '-0.1 %(0.10) to -4.8 %(0.40)'.

findings.claim: All 18 rows are hand transcriptions from a remote log (_source: 'kgy log transcription (esp-Z590, ~/sdcp/phase_ledger)') and omit every convention field the production writer emits for exactly this purpose: bridge_um, sdcp_sphere_d_um, origin_shift_um and vol_by_sid_um3 are all absent. The consequence is observable, not hypothetical: the report tool prints a warning on every one of the 18 rows that it is ASSUMING the SDCP diameter. Because ratio_to_true is computed against a hard-coded Ø0.30 true volume, a run made at a different SDCP_D would still print 0.984 and nothing in the chain would catch it — and 0.986/0.984/0.984 is the whole of the CL-39 STEP 1 'the mechanism variable has converged' verdict.
findings.evidence: Writer schema, scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py:1648-1660, emits {'vox_um','origin_shift_um','bridge_um','sdcp_yield_to_vgcf','sdcp_bridge_um','ptfe_block_um','ptfe_block_scope','ptfe_block_cells','sdcp_sphere_d_um','grid_shape','cells_by_sid','vol_by_sid_um3'}. The 18 committed rows contain only {_source, vox_um, grid_shape, cells_by_sid} (+ sphere_extra_from_sid, sphere_extra_cells on the six _sph rows). Running `python3 scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py --dir docs/data/prereg_v2/phase_ledger` prints on every row: 'SDCP representation/true volume = 0.984 (Ø 0.3 um  WARNING: no diameter recorded in row -> assuming default 0.30)'. Corroborating source: scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger.sh:45-47 documents the same gap in its own words ('the report sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py does not read bridge_um/sdcp_sphere_d_um from the ledger either, so there is no after-the-fact gate'). Mitigations that do exist and limit severity: the runner's defaults are BRIDGE_UM=0.48 / SDCP_D=0.30 and non-default values get a _b###/_d### filename suffix, so the unsuffixed names imply defaults; and scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger_match.py:same() is fail-closed on a missing field, so a re-run would recompute rather than silently reuse.
findings.proposed_action: Backfill bridge_um: 0.48 and sdcp_sphere_d_um (0.0 for _pt rows, 0.30 for _sph rows) into all 18 rows so the convention is recorded rather than inferred from the filename, or re-emit them from the rasterizer (CPU-only, minutes). Then teach sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py to read those fields instead of assuming 0.30, so the assumption warning becomes a check.

findings.claim: The aggregate file's own provenance header under-scopes the data it now depends on. _raw_ledgers says 'ledger_*.json — kgy log transcription (all 10 have per-phase sums exactly equal to the grid total cell count = transcription check passed)' and _how records the invocation as VOXES="0.4 0.3 0.25 0.15". The directory holds 18, and eight of them (vox 0.125 and 0.1, both beds, both stamps) are outside both that count and that invocation — yet the same file's sphere_stamp_grid_convergence and dof_measured sections are built entirely from six of those eight. So the file's transcription-check warrant covers 10 rows while its newest verdict rests on rows 11-18. I re-ran the check over all 18: every one passes (sum of cells_by_sid == product of grid_shape), so the assertion is true but its stated scope is stale.

(10 ... transcription check passed)'; phase_ledger_grid.json:4 '_how': 'scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger.sh (VOXES="0.4 0.3 0.25 0.15")'. The same stale count is repeated in docs/reviews/sdcp_phase_displacement_20260818.md:10 and :45 ('10 files, all pass') and in claims.json CL-43's raw-data line, so the documented reproduce command now yields 18 rows where the prose says 10.
findings.proposed_action: Update _raw_ledgers to '18 files, all pass the transcription check' and extend _how to record the second invocation (VOXES="0.125 0.1", registered in docs/reviews/sdcp_next_prereg_v3_20260818.md:39). findings.claim: Nothing automated ever reads these 18 rows. The only reader is scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py, invoked by hand with --dir; its selftest (7/7) is wired into neither scripts/check_all.sh, nor scripts/check_method_discipline.py, nor .github/workflows/discipline.yml — only the sibling sdcp_phase_ledger_match.py --selftest is. So the tool that turns these cell counts into the 0.986/0.984/0.984 convergence verdict has no standing regression, while claims.json cites '(selftest 7/7)' as part of the warrant.
findings.evidence: grep for 'sdcp_phase_ledger_report' in scripts/check_all.sh, scripts/check_method_discipline.py and .github/workflows/ returns nothing; the same grep for 'sdcp_phase_ledger_match' returns check_all.sh:55, check_method_discipline.py:793 and discipline.yml:60. scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py:192,242,250 do define a --selftest printing 'selftest {ok}/7 PASS'. findings.proposed_action: Add `run 'sdcp_phase_ledger_report --selftest' python3 scripts/sdcp_phase_ledger_report.py --selftest` to scripts/check_all.sh next to line 55, and register it in check_method_discipline.py's entrypoint list so CI covers it like the matcher.

verdict: This is a dead one-off sensitivity sweep: five STEP3 voxel-FV runs from 2026-07-15/17 on one 3.18 mAh DBE bed (case 260714_145738_778fa4) where only the sigma_SDCP entry of the material table changed, plus a derived 5-row summary. It is the raw material behind the retracted "+52.0 % / sigma_e 3.002" SDCP headline. It is NOT the canonical copy of anything live: claims.json CL-61 (status live, 2026-09-03) names this exact series and says do not revive the numbers, the sphere-stamp vox <= 0.15 axis supersedes it, and the replacement is already registered (docs/reviews/sdcp_inert_prereg_20260903.md sigma_SDCP=0 arm, plus the closure sweep's C2 axis which spans 2.5 to 25000 S/cm) though not yet executed. No script, plot, notebook or CI job reads any of these five files - every reference is doc prose. A v3 reorganization should archive the directory under an explicit HISTORICAL status marker rather than delete it (it is the only committed evidence of the sigma_SDCP dependence shape and the only source of the viewer's current-focusing reference values), and must fix the readers before it moves anything: the four JSONs are honest raw records that self-declare vox_um 0.4 and trust RELATIVE_v1 and sit inside a glob the ban sweep already reads, but sweep_summary.csv is a genuine unchecked leak - it carries the retracted headline as a bare vs_SBE_pct value 52.0, labels the row "anchor confirmed", omits any vox column, and lives outside BAN_SCAN_GLOBS, while three unbannered live documents quote the series from it, one of them (docs/litdb_application_table.md) being the webapp-v3 scoping table itself.

verdict: This is one family, not two: a single 32-arm decision-audit package for the manuscript's electronic-conductivity axis, split into two 19-file cohort directories that differ in exactly one registered axis (ptfe_stamp centerline vs off). Every file is a reduced STEP3 arm payload or its seal — 32 arms at vox 0.15 with sphere-stamped SDCP Ø0.30 under the p2-occupied-surface-first plate rule, code_sha c2f5b047, 8 pre-registered half-voxel grid-origin phases × 2 beds, all 32 converged (cg_info 0), σ_ion deliberately absent (LEAN=2, --no-ion --no-pore). It is the canonical, still-current copy: it is what released the σ_e HOLD on 2026-08-29 (table_s3_data_20260827.md header), and I reproduced its headline values exactly from the files themselves — paired R̄ = 1.307820 [1.301727, 1.310447] and 1.123672 [1.119994, 1.126646], mean σ_e 53.99 / 70.61 and 72.32 / 81.26 mS cm⁻¹, with all 16 out_sha256 plus both receipt_sha256 still matching and dropped=[] on all 32. Nothing here is superseded: the vox 0.125 cohorts in docs/data/cohorts/ are a documented non-convergence companion, not a replacement (Table S3 §11-3 explicitly declines to claim grid convergence and reports vox 0.15), and the p1-plate-rule values that CL-33/CL-41/CL-58 hold under quotation_ban are a different generation — I ran all 22 ban patterns over all 38 files and got zero hits, so carries_banned_value is false throughout. Archiving is not an option for any of these: check_cohort_packages.py re-derives both ratios from the arms on every `bash scripts/check_all.sh`, sdcp_gain_verdict.py reads the directories by name, claims.json CL-86 (2026-09-08) reads eight of the centerline pairs, and reduce_arm_payloads.py:461 uses docs/data/w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827/p2_SBE_sph_a0.json as its manifest fixture in a selftest that runs in CI on every push — moving or renaming that one file breaks the build. What v3 should do is leave the bytes alone and fix the thin layer around them: give the package a bed field so it stops depending on filenames and one script's hardcoded digest table (finding #1, the only one above P2), add a standing hash check so the ledger's integrity sentence stays true through a reorganization (#5), retire the retracted 표준오차/SE wording from the two receipts (#2), correct the one-digit range slip that the Figure 4b generator transcribes (#3), and make the figure tooling read these directories instead of a bit-identical ion8 sibling (#4). None of the five needs outside scientific judgement.

findings.claim: The sealed audit package cannot say, from its own contents, which arm is SBE and which is DBE — the one fact that sets the direction of the manuscript's headline ratio. Bed identity survives only as a substring in the filename plus a hardcoded dict in one script.
findings.evidence: Data file: run_receipt.json holds arms/bridge_um/code_sha/expect_backend/fibre_stamp/origins/periodic_xy/ptfe_stamp/receipt_digest/sdcp_sphere_d_um/sdcp_stamp/sdcp_yield_to_vgcf/vox_um — no bed or kit field. In the arm payloads, step3.manifest.input_files is {fibre, fibre_dia, metrics_json, phase, scaffold, se} = six bare 16-hex digests with no paths. CONTRADICTING SOURCE: scripts/check_cohort_packages.py:42-70 — "⚠⚠ 패키지는 자기가 어느 침대인지 말하지 못한다. run_receipt 에 침대가 없고 input_files 는 해시뿐이라 경로도 없다 … 16팔의 _SBE_/_DBE_ 를 전부 맞바꾸면 내부 일관성이 유지된 채 비가 1.123672 → 0.889944 로 뒤집히고 오류가 나지 않았다 (Codex 가 독립 재현했고 나도 재현했다) … 근본 해법은 러너가 receipt 에 침대를 적는 것이다. 그때까지 이 표가 유일한 앵커다." Second corroborating source that the direction is a live error surface: claims.json CL-86 (2026-09-08) ⓐ — "비 방향 DBE/SBE = 1.30782, SBE/DBE = 0.7646 ⇒ 원고 표기 뒤집힘", i.e. the direction was in fact written backwards in the Methods draft. The current labels are correct: the digest→bed registry (04b5a565ff4069f4=SBE, d1022e090ab625a9=DBE) is fail-closed, and the physics corroborates it independently — centerline vs off gives SBE −25.34 % and DBE −13.11 %, matching CL-49's −25.2 / −13.0 for 1 wt% vs 0.5 wt% PTFE. So this is an unclosed root cause with a working compensating control, not a wrong number.
findings.proposed_action: Have the runner write the bed label (and ideally the kit path) into run_receipt.json, and have reduce_arm_payloads.py copy it into each arm's _reduced block; then let check_cohort_packages.py cross-check receipt-bed against BED_DIGESTS against filename (three independent sources instead of two). Until then, open a findings.json item for it — the gap is documented only inside one script's comments, nowhere in findings.json, claims.json or any review doc, so a v3 reorganization has no ledger record telling it that these filenames are load-bearing.

findings.claim: Both committed verdict receipts print the ratio spread as a "표준오차 / SE", a framing the canonical ledger retracted for these very runs. The numbers are right; the label is the retracted one, and it survives verbatim in the artifact a third party is told to read.
findings.evidence: Data file, lines 26-27: "비의 상대 표준오차 = 0.3027 % (문턱 1.17 %, 비대응 = 게이트 규약) = 절대 0.3959 %p" and "쌍대응(origin-key join) 평균 = 1.30782 · SE = 0.0805 % · n = 8" (same at docs/data/w4b_ptfe_off_20260827/verdict_receipt.txt:26-27, 0.2701 % / SE 0.0849 %). CONTRADICTING SOURCE: docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:40-43 — "⚠ 별건 — 판정기 출력이 아직 표준오차 / SE 라고 적는다. R8 Q1 이 원고 표현으로는 철회한 말이다 (8 origin 은 한 침대의 완전 factorial → 복제 오차 자유도 0). 숫자는 origin-phase spread 로 맞고 라벨만 낡았다. 원고·이 문서는 이미 고쳤고, 도구 라벨 교체는 별도 항목으로 둔다." Same retraction is enforced in scripts/fig4b_sigma_conventions.py (docstring ②: "⚠ 표준오차·신뢰구간을 암시하는 어떤 표기도 쓰지 않는다"; CAPTION: "the band is not a standard error and no confidence interval is implied"). The ledger says the tool-label swap is deferred to "별도 항목", but no such item exists — grepping docs/reviews/findings.json for 표준오차 returns only CDXR2-3, which is the different relative-%-vs-%p issue and is already claimed_fixed at 080dd92e.
findings.proposed_action: Rename the two output lines in scripts/sdcp_gain_verdict.py from 표준오차/SE to origin-phase spread (keeping the numbers and the gate input unchanged, as CDXR2-3 did with aliases), regenerate the two verdict_receipt.txt files, and file the deferred item in findings.json so the ledger's "별도 항목으로 둔다" points at something real.

findings.claim: The ledger's observed-range row for the centerline cohort is off by one in the last digit at both ends, and that wrong pair — not the correct one that also exists in the repo — is what the Figure 4b generator transcribes into the published band.
findings.evidence: Data: the 16 sigma_e values in this receipt give paired ratios spanning 1.301726808 (SBE/DBE a6) to 1.310446940 (SBE/DBE a4), i.e. 1.301727 – 1.310447 to six places. CONTRADICTING SOURCE: docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:123 (canonical ledger) says "관측 범위 1.301726 – 1.310448", repeated at docs/reviews/codex_r8_verdict_20260827.md:34, and transcribed into scripts/fig4b_sigma_conventions.py:35 as lo=1.301726, hi=1.310448. The correct pair is present elsewhere in the same repo: docs/session_20260902_progress.md:150 prints "R 1.307820 [1.301727, 1.310447]" and docs/reviews/ion_ptfe_sign_prereg_20260830.md:176 prints the full "1.301726808 – 1.310446940". The off row is unaffected (table_s3:172 "1.119994 – 1.126646" rounds correctly from 1.119993954 / 1.126645993), and the percent column of the same centerline row is correct (30.173 – 31.045 % vs computed 30.1727 / 31.0447), so the slip is confined to the ratio column of one row. Magnitude ~1e-6; no physical consequence.
findings.proposed_action: Fix docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:123 and scripts/fig4b_sigma_conventions.py:35 to 1.301727 / 1.310447, and note the correction at docs/reviews/codex_r8_verdict_20260827.md:34. Better: have fig4b_sigma_conventions.py derive lo/hi/ratio/spread from docs/data/w4*/ at build time instead of hardcoding, which removes this transcription hop entirely.

findings.claim: The manifest seals 16 out_sha256 plus receipt_sha256 and the ledger cites that as a closed integrity property, but no committed check ever re-verifies those hashes — the exact one-shot-verification failure mode the checker that does run was written to prevent.
findings.evidence: Data file: cohort_manifest.json carries out_sha256 for all 16 arms and receipt_sha256 for run_receipt.json (I verified today that 16/16 + the receipt still match on both directories, and dropped=[] everywhere). CONTRADICTING SOURCE: docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:20-21 asserts "무결성: out_sha256 16/16 × 2 일치 · run_receipt 해시 일치" as a settled fact, while scripts/check_cohort_packages.py — the only standing repo-mode reader, wired at scripts/check_all.sh:135 — contains no hashlib and no sha256 comparison (its only sha256 mention, :200, merely asserts _reduced.source_sha256 is non-empty); .github/workflows/discipline.yml runs only the --selftest variants. The same script's own docstring states the design intent it fell short of: "그것은 2026-08-29 에 손으로 한 번 돌린 결과였고 그 뒤로 아무것도 다시 확인하지 않는다. 누가 패키지를 건드리거나 판정기가 바뀌면 원장의 그 문장이 조용히 거짓이 된다." It closed the ratio↔ledger half and left the bytes↔manifest half open. Partial mitigation exists: sdcp_gain_verdict.py recomputes physics_protocol_id from the manifest, so an edit to a physics axis breaks the seal, and an edited sigma_e would break the ratio comparison.
findings.proposed_action: Add an out_sha256 / receipt_sha256 verification pass to check_cohort_packages.py's repo-mode loop (a dozen lines, no solve, already-present manifest fields). This matters specifically for the v3 reorganization: a re-serialization, a line-ending renormalization or a path move is exactly what would silently invalidate the ledger's integrity sentence today.

findings.claim: The 16 centerline sigma_e values exist bit-identically in five committed directories, and the figure CSV that publishes them is regenerated by default from one of the four non-canonical copies rather than from the sealed W4 package the ledger names as their provenance.
findings.evidence: Measured: for all 16 arms, sigma_e_eff_S_cm and n_dof are bit-identical between docs/data/w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827/ and each of docs/data/ion8_isd0_20260831/, ion8_isd10e-03_20260831/, ion8_isd521007e-04_20260831/, ion8_isd55216e-05_20260831/ (16/16 each); ion8_isd10e-03 even carries the identical physics_protocol_id p2-9cd29a0c61085621, differing only in code_sha (657c2192 vs c2f5b047) and in solving the ionic axis as well. Running scripts/check_cohort_packages.py prints ratio 1.307820 and "σ_e SBE 53.99 · DBE 70.61" for all five. CONTRADICTING SOURCE: docs/reviews/table_s3_data_20260827.md:5-8 names docs/data/w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827/ (with w4b) as THE committed provenance for the sigma_e axis, yet scripts/plot_sigma_e_bars.py:91 sets `--dir` default to docs/data/ion8_isd0_20260831, so the committed docs/figures/sigma_e_bars.csv (row 2: SBE,0,54.530440; row 10: DBE,0,71.400440 — exactly this arm pair) reproduces from a different directory. The bit-identity is itself recorded at docs/reviews/handoff_20260831_manuscript_track.md:121. Nothing here is wrong; the risk is that the five copies have different code_sha and different ionic-axis settings, so "which one is the source" has five answers.
findings.proposed_action: Point scripts/plot_sigma_e_bars.py's default --dir at docs/data/w4_ptfe_centerline_20260827 (the ledger-named provenance) and note in a v3 data index that ion8_* are supersets of the same electronic solve differing only in σ_ion(SDCP). Do NOT delete any copy — the ion8 quartet is CL-59's identifiability evidence and the bit-identity across them is itself a published negative control. Note the CSV-lacks-a-provenance-header half of this overlaps a finding already registered in docs/data/audit_20260909/audit1_scopes.json.

surface_worthy.why: These two directories jointly hold the manuscript's Figure 4b / Table S3 electronic payload — the 4 × 8 per-origin σ_e table for two beds under two binder conventions — and today the only way to see it is to parse 32 JSONs or read a Korean verdict receipt. A v3 hub reader looking for "the σ_e numbers" currently lands on a figure CSV that carries arm 0 only, with no convention label and no provenance line.
surface_worthy.one_line: σ_e at vox 0.15, sphere-stamped SDCP, 8 grid-origin phases × {SBE, DBE} × {PTFE off, PTFE centerline}: off 72.32 / 81.26 mS cm⁻¹ (R = 1.123672), centerline 53.99 / 70.61 (R = 1.307820), all 32 arms converged (cg_info 0).

surface_worthy.why: The two receipts differ in exactly one field (ptfe_stamp off vs centerline) out of thirteen, and I confirmed the 32 arms match on every other axis — code_sha c2f5b047, vox 0.15, bridge 0.48, dilate_z 1.0719, seed 3, σ table, plate rule p2-occupied-surface-first, and the same two input_digests per bed. That single-axis cleanliness is the whole reason the pair can be subtracted, and it is nowhere stated as a checked fact; the reader is left to trust it.
surface_worthy.one_line: A verified single-axis contrast: the PTFE-off and PTFE-centerline cohorts are identical in all 13 sealed run axes and all 55 manifest keys except ptfe_stamp, so their difference isolates the binder-blocking convention alone.

surface_worthy.why: The binder-blocking asymmetry falls straight out of these two directories and is a headline-grade physical result, but it is not tabulated side by side anywhere — it is only reachable by differencing two cohorts. It also independently corroborates the bed labelling (finding #1) and confirms CL-49's prediction on a full 8-origin factorial instead of a single arm.
surface_worthy.one_line: Blocking the PTFE centerline costs the 1 wt%-binder SBE −25.3 % of its electronic conductivity but the 0.5 wt% DBE only −13.1 %, which is why the reported ratio moves from 1.1237 to 1.3078 — the convention choice, not the physics, sets the magnitude.

surface_worthy.why: This is the answer to "how do I know these numbers came from the 2026-08-27 recompacted beds?", and it is buried in a manifest nobody opens. It is also the honest statement of what is NOT reproducible from the repo: the 2.10 GB of raw payload per cohort was never committed, so the package supports re-deriving the judgement but not re-running the solver.
surface_worthy.one_line: Provenance chain for the σ_e axis: 16 arms reduced 131 MB → 5.8 kB each with dropped=[], src_sha256 pinned to the kgy originals (2.10 GB per cohort, not in the repo), receipt_sha256 sealing the runner intent, and per-bed input_digest 04b5a565ff4069f4 (SBE) / d1022e090ab625a9 (DBE).

verdict: This bucket is not one family — it is four unrelated leftovers that the scope globs each claimed and nobody opened, and three of the four are load-bearing. (1) `docs/data/cbd_contacts_20260831/` is LIVE canonical manuscript data: two JSONs holding all 1,271 per-AM contact counts per bed, read by scripts/plot_cbd_contacts.py (CI-selftested) into docs/figures/cbd_contacts.* and thence into the manuscript table in ms_readthrough_20260903.md, whose every percentile I reproduced exactly from the raw counts. Keep them, do not archive; but they violate the live CL-75 rule (no code_sha/argv/date in the file, and the producer emits none), and their live reader expects a convention key (`include_ptfe`) the producer never writes, so the convention line prints None for both the 74→86 and the 80→88 conventions while the selftest stays green on an invented fixture key. (2) `docs/data/angular_risk/` is HISTORICAL, not live: Codex R9 marked the screen Q3 REFUTED the same week (non-periodic KDTree, pre-STEP2 additive-free inputs, corrected p05 0.39985 → 0.46700 / K 8 → 7), CL-79 ordered a re-measurement that has not happened, and neither the files nor the doc that indexes them nor the still-live CL-76 carries that banner. Worse, the kit file is bit-identical in all 27 measured keys to docs/data/phase_a_6mah/angular_risk.json, and their input scaffolds differ only in a header comment — so what the ledger treats as two beds' screens (CL-76 kit, CL-78 Phase A) is one measurement, and the Phase A README's claim that its bed is \"NOT the old campaign bed\" plus its additive-count reconciliation are unsupported as independent evidence. v3 should keep one copy (the clean-provenance one here, code_dirty false), delete the code_dirty:true twin, and banner both. (3) `docs/data/audit_20260909/` is LIVE audit infrastructure, correct in substance — missed.json's 843 paths are unique, all tracked, and exactly the union of buckets.json — but buckets.json still carries three alias buckets from an expired in-flight compatibility fix, so it reads as 97 buckets / 888 slots against the 94 / 843 every doc states, and next week's resume instruction (\"buckets.json 에서 위 8 개를 빼면 나온다\") would re-schedule 45 already-finished files. (4) webapp/requirements.txt is LIVE (scripts/setup_gabia.sh) and near-clean; one orphan (`tabulate`) and no pins. Nothing in this bucket is a dead one-off sweep and nothing here should be archived — the correct v3 move is the opposite: two of these families (cbd contacts, audit coverage) belong on the hub's front page, and the angular_risk pair needs a retraction marker before anyone finds it there.

findings.claim: This file and docs/data/phase_a_6mah/angular_risk.json are the SAME measurement — all 27 measured keys are bit-identical — yet the ledger counts them as screens of two different beds, and the copy the Phase A docs cite is the one its own gate forbids quoting.
findings.evidence: Key-by-key diff: every measured key is equal (n_particles 1498, cov_p05 0.39985000000000004, cov_mean 0.5688928571428572, H_p95 112.44892314169918, K_required_from_p05 8, all three z_bins). Only label/am_csv/se_csv/provenance differ. The inputs are also identical: `gunzip -c docs/data/phase_a_6mah/am_scaffold.csv.gz` vs `docs/data/kit_ps_scaffolds/kit_ps_7_3__am_scaffold.csv.gz` differ in exactly 2 lines — both the header comment (`case input_6mAh_real_4` vs `case 260421_215212_f0b6df`, which docs/data/case_master.csv:51 maps to each other) — with all 1,498 AM and 158,688 SE rows equal. Contradicting sources: docs/data/phase_a_6mah/README.md:17 asserts "⚠ 이것은 옛 캠페인 침대가 **아니다** — 같은 설계점의 새 realization 이다", and claims.json CL-78 provenance (line 2098) says the user supplied a "**새 DEM 산출물**"; CL-78 then reports the Phase A screen (K_required = 8) as one of "사전계산 3건" while CL-76 separately reports the kit screen. README.md:26-36 additionally offers an additive-count reconciliation ("넷 중 셋이 네 자리까지 일치 … 이 실측 침대가 옛 캠페인을 더 잘 재현한다") as evidence of fidelity to the lost old bed — which is arithmetic, not validation, if the coordinates are the same rows.
findings.proposed_action: Record in CL-78 / phase_a_6mah/README.md that the Phase A scaffold is row-identical to the pre-loss kit_ps_7_3 scaffold (either a deterministic re-run of the same deck+seed 80363, or a re-export of the surviving copy) and therefore (a) the additive-count reconciliation is not independent evidence and (b) the Phase A angular screen is not a second bed's screen. Then delete or symlink one of the two angular_risk JSONs; keep the clean-provenance one here (code_dirty false) and drop the code_dirty:true twin, which also closes Codex R9 ④ ('내 게이트가 인용 금지라고 적어둔 파일을 README·prereg·CL-78 에서 인용했다') at zero cost.

findings.claim: The file's headline numbers (cov_p05 0.39985, K_required_from_p05 = 8) were refuted the same week by Codex R9 as periodic-blind and non-transferable, with a corrected value on record — but the file carries no marker, the doc that indexes it still lists it as a sealed output, and CL-76 is still `live` reporting K = 8~12.
findings.evidence: File line 4/18: `"cov_p05": 0.39985000000000004` and `"K_required_from_p05": 8`. Contradicting source: docs/reviews/codex_r9_verdict_phase_a_20260907.md:131-141 ('Q3 REFUTED — 각도 선별은 전이되지 않고, 봉인이 인용을 금지한다'): the tool reads only additive-free rigid AM/SE CSVs, not STEP2 se_dump/phase/fibre; production is x/y periodic but the screening KDTree has no periodic images, and an independent 9-image recompute gives `p05 0.39985 → 0.46700, K 8 → 7`; conclusion '네 조성 모두의 최종 STEP2 상태에서 periodic-aware 선별을 다시 해야 한다'. Adopted into the live ledger as CL-79 ④ and CL-79 verdict '남은 것: … angular_risk 재측정(네 조성 post-STEP2 · periodic-aware · 깨끗한 트리)'. Yet CL-76 (status live, same date) still states '사전등록 규칙이 K = 8~12 를 준다' with no mention of periodic or CL-79, and docs/reviews/replay_and_angular_screen_20260907.md:14-17 still lists the file under '봉인된 산출물' with no banner.
findings.proposed_action: Add a superseded/hold marker inside the JSON (the repo already has the pattern: the retired step3_transport_resolution _v2.json carries a `superseded_by` key), amend CL-76 with the CL-79 refutation and the periodic-aware p05 0.46700 / K 7, and banner docs/reviews/replay_and_angular_screen_20260907.md §봉인된 산출물. Record that the screen is non-periodic and pre-STEP2 in the file's `assumptions` string, which currently names only the coverage-gap and I∝V conventions.

findings.claim: Both cbd_contacts JSONs carry a manuscript number and have no commit SHA, no argv, no run directory and no date — exactly what the live resident rule CL-75 says makes a measurement JSON uncitable — and the producing script emits no provenance at all, so re-running will not fix it.
findings.evidence: Neither docs/data/cbd_contacts_20260831/contacts_DBE_band015.json nor contacts_SBE_band015.json contains `code_sha`, `code_dirty`, `argv`, `utc` or a bed path; the top level is only {summary, convention, counts} per convention key. scripts/cbd_contacts_per_am.py:272 builds the convention as `dict(band_um=..., kinds=..., n_am=..., ...)` and :470 dumps `res` — no provenance emitter exists. Contradicting source: claims.json CL-75 (status live, 2026-09-07) '⇒ **상주 규칙 신설: 측정 JSON 은 그것을 만든 커밋 SHA 를 자기 안에 적는다.  없으면 인용하지 않는다.**' — a rule the sibling angular_risk files obey, including the note '`code_sha` 가 없거나 `code_dirty` 가 참이면 수치를 인용하지 말 것 (CL-75)'. Meanwhile these files ARE being cited: docs/reviews/ms_readthrough_20260903.md:327-340 derives the manuscript table from them and records '저자는 ⑥ 에 `85 %` 만 넣기로 했다'. I reproduced that table exactly from the raw counts (p5 58→68 +17.2 %, p50 74→86 +16.2 %, p95 91→104 +14.3 %, min–max 42–106 / 55–118, 1083/1271 = 85.2 %, 631/1271 = 49.6 %), so the numbers are right — only their provenance is absent.
findings.proposed_action: Add a provenance emitter to scripts/cbd_contacts_per_am.py (the same block the angular_risk writer uses: code_sha, code_dirty, dirty_scope, branch, argv, utc) and re-run it on both beds to reseal contacts_{SBE,DBE}_band015.json before the 85 % / 74→86 numbers go into the manuscript. The re-run is CPU-only. Until then the manuscript citation is a live CL-75 violation.

findings.claim: The live reader expects a convention key `include_ptfe` that the producer never writes, so the convention line that is supposed to travel with these numbers prints `include_ptfe=None` for BOTH conventions — and the selftest is green because its fixture invents the key.
findings.evidence: The files' convention blocks contain `"kinds": ["VGCF", "SDCP"]` (and `["VGCF","SDCP","PTFE"]`) and no `include_ptfe`. scripts/plot_cbd_contacts.py:41 reads `this = (c.get('band_um'), c.get('include_ptfe'), c.get('representation'))` and :47 returns `include_ptfe=conv[1]`; :180 prints `규약: band {…} µm · include_ptfe={conv["include_ptfe"]}`. Running load() on the real files returns `include_ptfe: None` for both the conductive-only key (74→86) and the WITH_PTFE key (80→88) — verified by executing the loader. The producer, scripts/cbd_contacts_per_am.py:272, emits `kinds`, never `include_ptfe`. The selftest fixture at :203-206 writes `'include_ptfe': inc` into the convention, so the guard and the print are exercised only against a schema that never exists on disk — the fixture-vs-real false green CLAUDE.md discipline ⑤ describes. The stakes are named by the script's own docstring and by CLAUDE.md CL-49: '포함하면 80 → 88 로 달라진다'.
findings.proposed_action: Either have cbd_contacts_per_am.py write `include_ptfe` alongside `kinds`, or have plot_cbd_contacts.load() derive it from `kinds` ('PTFE' in kinds) and raise rather than print None. Change the selftest fixture to the producer's real schema (`kinds`) so the negative control tests what is actually written; the cross-bed convention guard currently checks only 2 of its 3 elements on real data.

findings.claim: The bucket file holds 97 keys and 888 path slots for 843 unique paths — three Korean-directory buckets appear twice, under both an octal-escaped key and a decoded key — while every doc that cites it says 94 buckets / 843 paths, and next week's resume plan is told to rebuild the remaining work from this file.
findings.evidence: Measured: 97 top-level keys, 888 total list entries, 843 unique; 45 paths appear in two buckets. The duplicate pairs are `'"\\354\\235\\264\\354\\242\\205\\352\\270\\260\\354\\210\\240#1'` ↔ `'이종기술#1'` (22 paths), #2 (22), #3 (1). The path VALUES are decoded in both. Contradicting sources: docs/session_20260909_progress.md:170-171 '버킷 정본 = docs/data/audit_20260909/buckets.json (94 버킷·843 경로)'; docs/data/audit_20260909/GAP_AUDIT_HOLD.md:27-28 '83 버킷 · 702 파일.  버킷 정본은 같은 폴더 buckets.json (94 버킷 전체).  남은 목록은 buckets.json 에서 위 8 개를 빼면 나온다' and :52 '다음 주에는 buckets.json 에서 다시 만든다'. Applying that subtraction rule literally to the committed file yields 89 buckets / 747 unique paths, not 83 / 702 — it silently re-schedules the 45 Korean files that wf_1c515e69-883 already finished, and double-assigns each of them. Commit 5ebdb2e72's message documents the aliases as deliberate ('agents already in flight were dispatched with the escaped key and a rename would have failed their lookup mid-run') — a reason that expired when that run ended, and one that lives only in the commit message, not the file.
findings.proposed_action: Drop the three octal-escaped alias keys now that no run is in flight (leaving 94 keys / 843 slots, matching every doc), or add a `_done` / `_alias_of` field inside the file so the resume script can subtract completed buckets mechanically instead of a human reading '위 8 개를 빼면'.

findings.claim: The coverage-accounting block states the repo has 1,879 tracked files; the measurement committed in the same folder on the same day says 1,882, and `git ls-tree` at the very commit that added this line also says 1,882.
findings.evidence: docs/session_20260909_progress.md:135 'git 추적 1,879   1차 감사 22 영역이 도달 가능 1,036   미도달 843   = 55.1 %  ← 주장(glob)' — i.e. the total is back-derived as 1,036 + 843. Contradicting sources: docs/data/audit_20260909/coverage.json `"tracked_files": 1882`; claims.json CL-89 (live, 2026-09-09) 'git 추적 파일  1,882'; and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 6d5e9207e | wc -l` = 1882 at the commit that introduced this very line. Three files that the globs claimed and the audit reached are therefore unaccounted for in the doc's arithmetic.
findings.proposed_action: Change 1,879 → 1,882 in the block and note that 1,036 + 843 does not close (3 files are in neither set), or drop the derived total and point at coverage.json, which is the measured artifact. Low stakes — the doc's header already says '충돌 시 원장과 사전등록이 이긴다' — but this is the one section whose whole subject is coverage arithmetic being reported as measured rather than claimed.

findings.claim: The real_14 half of the screening pair rests on the same refuted tool as the kit half — non-periodic KDTree, pre-STEP2 additive-free scaffolds — but unlike the kit file it has no corrected number on record, and it is still presented as a sealed current output.
findings.evidence: File lines 63-72 name the inputs `docs/data/real14_{am,se}_scaffold.csv` (rigid-sphere scaffolds, no STEP2 phase/fibre arrays) and the `assumptions` string records only the I∝V and coverage-gap conventions — no boundary convention. Contradicting source: docs/reviews/codex_r9_verdict_phase_a_20260907.md:135-137 ('도구는 **무첨가 강체 AM/SE CSV** 만 읽는다 … 생산은 **x/y periodic** 인데 선별 KDTree 에 **periodic image 가 없다**') and the adopted CL-79 action item 4 ('angular_risk 재측정 — 네 조성 post-STEP2 · periodic-aware · 깨끗한 트리에서 봉인'). Codex recomputed the periodic-aware p05 only for the kit bed (0.39985 → 0.46700); for real_14 (cov_p05 0.2584, K_required_from_p05 12 — the upper end of CL-76's live 'K = 8~12') no corrected value exists. docs/reviews/replay_and_angular_screen_20260907.md:16 still lists it under '봉인된 산출물' with no banner.
findings.proposed_action: Banner the file and the replay doc as pre-STEP2 / non-periodic, and either recompute real_14 with periodic images (CPU-only, scripts/step4_angular_risk.py) or state in CL-76 that the K=12 upper end is unverified under the production periodic convention. Also record the boundary convention in the file's `assumptions` string, as the sibling cbd_contacts convention block does.

findings.claim: `tabulate` is installed on every gabia webapp deploy and nothing in the repo imports it.
findings.evidence: webapp/requirements.txt:11 `tabulate`. A repo-wide grep for `import tabulate` / `from tabulate` over scripts/ and webapp/ returns nothing; the only occurrences of the string anywhere are the English word in prose (scripts/mpm_webapp_payload.py:948 'Do NOT tabulate it next to', docs/literature_coverage/README.md:61 'not tabulated'). Contradicting source: the requirements file is consumed for real at scripts/setup_gabia.sh:64, so this is an installed-but-unused dependency, not a scratch note. (Adjacent, deliberately not filed as a finding: PIL, weasyprint and pybamm are imported by webapp/app.py:7403, :9035 and webapp/pybamm_predictor.py:42 but absent from the manifest — all three sit inside try/except with a user-facing fallback message, so their omission is intentional.)
findings.proposed_action: Drop `tabulate`. While the file is open, consider pinning: it is unpinned except flask>=3.0 and last changed 2026-05-26, and it builds the server that renders user-facing figures and reports, where a silent matplotlib/numpy major bump changes output.

surface_worthy.why: This is the raw distribution behind a number the author has already decided to publish ("⑥ 에 85 % 만 넣기로 했다") and behind manuscript Fig 4b, yet it is discoverable only through a review handoff doc. It holds all 1,271 per-AM values, so the whole percentile table reproduces from it exactly — and it is the rare measurement in this repo that is convention-labelled inside the file (band 0.15 µm, distinct objects not points, outside-shell only, PTFE excluded), which is precisely what the number needs to travel with.
surface_worthy.one_line: Per-AM conductive-additive contacts, SBE vs DBE: medians 74 → 86 (+16 %), 85.2 % of DBE particles above the SBE median, whole distribution shifted with the lower tail gaining most — the raw evidence that the additive gain is not local.

surface_worthy.why: It is the only artifact that makes this repo's audit coverage a computed set difference rather than a claim, and CL-89 is the ledger entry saying that distinction is the point. A v3 hub that wants to answer "how much of this repo has actually been read" needs this list and its bucket partition surfaced, not buried under docs/data/.
surface_worthy.one_line: The 843 tracked paths the first exhaustive audit's hand-written scope globs never reached — verified unique, verified all still tracked, and exactly the union of buckets.json.

surface_worthy.why: It answers a question a reader will ask before any STEP4 campaign — "how many angular sectors does a pilot need, and are there particles with no ionic contact at all?" — with per-z-bin resolution, and it is cheap to recompute (scaffold CSVs only, no GPU). But it must be surfaced with the CL-79 refutation attached, or a reader will size a pilot from a screen the ledger says does not transfer.
surface_worthy.one_line: Per-particle coverage / angular-risk screen: no particle is uncontacted in either bed (zero fraction 0.0, H infinite 0), and the z-gradient is strong only in the thin bed — the opposite of the thickness hypothesis.
